s.t: Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

Our Product Managers imagine the ideal experience for our community and work backwards, creating innovative products that delight our guests and hosts. They deeply understand the needs of our users and translate these into a strategy that combines strong product thinking and deep research.

They partner with talented cross-functional team members across engineering, design, operations, data science, and more, leading teams to execute a shared vision. They are incredibly detail-oriented and hands on.

Airbnb is seeking an exceptional product manager to reimagine how guests search on Airbnb. Search is the front door to the entire guest experience — the moment someone tells us what they want and we have to understand it, then show them the right options in the right order. Today that means query understanding, filtering, and ranking.

Tomorrow it means next-generation AI capabilities that let guests search more naturally, get better matches with less effort, and trust that Airbnb understood what they were actually looking for.
In this role, you will own the vision and roadmap for the future of search at Airbnb — pushing beyond keyword and filter-based search toward more intelligent, conversational, and personalized ways for guests to find their perfect stay. You'll partner closely with engineering, design, and data science teams to bring new AI-powered search capabilities from concept to guests.
This is a high-visibility role building one of the most consequential surfaces in the guest experience, and will regularly interface with senior engineering and leadership stakeholders.

Define and drive the long-term vision and roadmap for the future of search on Airbnb, including next-generation AI capabilities like natural language and conversational search, query understanding, and intelligent ranking.
Own how guests search on Airbnb end to end — from the moment they express intent to the moment they find the right option.
Partner closely with engineering, applied ML, and data science teams to design, prototype, and ship AI-powered search experiences.
Use quantitative analysis and experimentation (A/B testing) to validate that new search capabilities improve relevance, conversion, and guest satisfaction.
Translate ambiguous guest problems into clear product requirements, prioritized against business impact and technical feasibility.
Collaborate with design and research to understand how guests search, filter, and decide today — and where AI can remove friction.
Work cross-functionally with Host-side and Trust teams to ensure smarter search continues to surface the right inventory fairly and accurately.
Communicate roadmap, results, and trade-offs clearly to engineering partners and leadership.

10+ years of consumer product management experience, with a track record of owning a product area end to end.
Experience working on search, discovery, ranking, or recommendation systems is strongly preferred.
Genuine excitement about applying modern AI and ML capabilities (LLMs, semantic search, conversational interfaces) to consumer product problems.
Strong business acumen and ability to use data, research, and experimentation to drive product strategy and decisions.
Demonstrated ability to work closely with ML/data science teams and understand the trade-offs of model-driven products.
Excellent problem-solving, communication, and collaboration skills across engineering, design, data science, and other cross-functional teams.
A user-centered mindset — you dig into how guests actually search and where they get stuck, not just metrics dashboards.

Due to the nature of this position, there is a strong preference for the successful applicant will need to be based in San Francisco, CA to be able to conduct their work. Currently, employees can not be located in: Alaska, Indiana, Nebraska, North Dakota, Ohio, South Dakota, Wisconsin, Alabama, Mississippi, Oklahoma, Delaware And Rhode Island.

Who we are
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet.
Stripe Apps connect Stripe with the tools businesses already use, bringing relevant data and workflows into the Stripe Dashboard and third-party systems. The Strategic Apps team owns a portfolio of integrations with enterprise systems that are critical to our users’ workflows—from quote-to-cash and support to reporting. We help users embed Stripe more deeply into the way they run their businesses.

We’re looking for a Staff Product Manager to set the strategy and lead execution for Strategic Apps. You will own a portfolio of existing and new integrations, including those with systems such as Salesforce, and determine where Stripe should invest based on user needs, Stripe’s product and industry priorities, and market signals. You will work across Stripe and directly with external partners to deliver reliable, high-quality integrations that drive adoption and business outcomes.
Own the vision, product strategy, roadmap, and success metrics for a portfolio of strategic apps, making and communicating clear trade-offs amid significant ambiguity.
Identify, prioritize, and validate the highest-value user problems and integration opportunities through direct user research, ecosystem analysis, and quantitative evidence.
Lead cross-functional teams across Engineering, Design, Data Science, Finance, Sales, User Support, Marketing, Partner Management, and other product teams to deliver and evolve integrations end to end.
Partner with Engineering to define product requirements, technical approach, and quality standards for integrations, including APIs, documentation, edge cases, reliability, security, compliance, and ongoing maintenance.
Establish feedback loops and measurement plans before launch; use product, business, and user metrics to assess efficacy, diagnose changes in performance, and continuously improve adoption, retention, and revenue outcomes.
Represent Stripe’s product strategy with strategic technology partners and enterprise users, building productive relationships with product and technical counterparts and incorporating their feedback into roadmap decisions.
Drive launches, beta programs, user acceptance testing, and go-to-market readiness in partnership with Marketing, Sales, Partner Management, and Support; ensure teams have the materials and operating model needed to support adoption at scale.
Make and drive important cross-functional decisions, align senior stakeholders around a shared strategy, and communicate progress, risks, and outcomes clearly.
Balance new feature development with investment in quality, reliability, technical debt, and foundational platform capabilities across the app portfolio.
Improve how Stripe builds and operates strategic integrations by turning user, partner, and performance signals into scalable product and process improvements.

8+ years of relevant product-management, engineering, or equivalent experience, including ownership of a high-quality product or feature area at scale or a major evolution of an existing product.
Experience setting product strategy and driving execution across multiple cross-functional teams or a complex product area, from ambiguous problem definition through launch and iteration.
Demonstrated ability to use qualitative and quantitative evidence to define success metrics, evaluate product performance, and make prioritization decisions.
Strong technical judgment and fluency working with engineers on API-based products, integrations, technical constraints, and product quality.
Experience engaging directly with enterprise users and external technology partners, and translating their needs into clear product decisions.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a track record of influencing senior stakeholders and leading through organizational boundaries.

Experience with enterprise business systems and workflows, such as CRM, ERP, quote-to-cash, support, or reporting platforms; familiarity with Salesforce, Oracle, SAP, or Microsoft Dynamics is a plus.
Experience building or scaling platform, ecosystem, marketplace, or partner-integrated products.
Experience growing product adoption, usage, or revenue through product-led and go-to-market initiatives.
Experience in payments, financial technology, or other regulated technology environments.
A degree in computer science, engineering, or another technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies, from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups, use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

Stripe's Professional Services (ProServ) team helps businesses around the world design, implement, and optimise their Stripe integrations. As we scale our global delivery capability, we are building a structured portfolio of service offerings that define the scope, methodology, resourcing, and commercial terms of how we engage with our users.

We are looking for a Product Manager ( Professional Services) to own the portfolio of offerings end-to-end. The role sits at the intersection of services strategy, commercial design, and delivery operations. You will be the person who determines whether our offerings are well-designed, effectively sold, and profitably delivered and you will take action to refine the portfolio as needed.
This is not a traditional Product Manager role, but it demands the same rigour. Your "product" is the service itself: its scope, its pricing, its methodology, and its performance. You will work closely with Sales, Delivery, Finance, and Stripe's Product organisation to ensure that every offering in our portfolio is fit for purpose and continuously improving.

Own the offering portfolio for Professional Services
Maintain and govern ProServ’s offering portfolio including scope, hours, pricing, and resource plans for each offering. Our portfolio includes offerings designed for all user segments from start-ups to enterprises
Manage the full offering lifecycle: design, build, launch, iterate, and deprecate offerings based on market need, delivery performance, and product roadmap changes
Ensure the portfolio stays current as Stripe launches new products
Design and implement a governance framework for the portfolio of offerings
Drive offering performance analytics
Define and track the offering KPIs: attach rate, average scope deviation, planned vs. actual burn rate, gross margin per offering, and customer satisfaction
Run regular performance reviews and present findings to ProServ leadership with clear recommendations
Refine and Improve Offering Design
Analyse delivery burn data to identify offerings that are systematically over- or under-scoped, and propose refinements
Conduct structured retrospectives with Delivery Leads after engagement close to capture insights and feedback
Serve as the structured feedback loop between Delivery (what is hard to deliver), Sales (what is hard to sell), and Finance (what is margin-accretive), synthesising those inputs into offering design decisions

Required

Demonstrable experience shaping or owning a service offering
Commercial literacy
Strong analytical skills
Excellent written communication
Product Management training or experience
The ability to apply product thinking (hypothesis, prototype, measure, iterate) to service design

Familiarity with Certinia and/or Salesforce
Exposure to partner and SI ecosystem dynamics

TwoTwenty is Pinterest's incubation team. We invented Shuffles and Collages and we're the team behind Beauty Guides, Restyle and Smart Blocks. We're hiring a product manager to own one of our shipping products end to end, or to lead one of our next zero-to-one bets from a blank page to real users.

Own a product on TwoTwenty end to end, from strategy through post-launch iteration. You'll pick between a substantial slice of the teams AI Experiences charter or one of the team's next bets in areas like generative creation tools, live shopping or AI planning surfaces.
Make the product decisions that separate a demo from a product. You'll decide what ships in V1, defend the cut list and set the quality bar on your surface so designers and engineers calibrate to it.
Land launches that require alignment with partner teams inside Pinterest (AIFwd, Search, Shop with Pinterest, ATG). You'll get to agreement without needing your manager in the room.
Translate a company-level thesis into a concrete product decision your team can build against. You'll be able to state your product's strategy in one sentence and connect this week's engineering work to it.
Run experiments that answer real questions, not experiments that produce metrics. You'll decide when a null result is a launch signal and when a positive result isn't good enough.
Use AI to accelerate exploration, drafting and analysis in your day-to-day. This includes prototyping concepts, comparing design options and synthesizing user research, while applying judgment and verification to protect correctness and quality.
Mentor at least one PM or designer on the team on the craft of narrowing a problem before writing the doc.

Minimum of 6 years of product management experience, including shipping a consumer product with an AI or ML component to at least one million users.
Experience owning a zero-to-one product from a blank page through real user traffic, not a prototype in a deck.
Experience saying no to a well-liked feature request from an executive and holding the line on quality.
Experience earning the trust of a senior engineering leader on architectural decisions, and can describe how you did it.
Understanding of the difference between a strategy and a plan, and the ability to state your current team's strategy in one sentence.
Experience using AI to accelerate product exploration, competitive analysis or user research synthesis, with a clear approach to validating accuracy and quality before decisions get made.
Committed to owning outcomes end to end. You treat things outside your scope as yours when the product needs it, and you don't lean on process to make decisions the team is looking to you for.
Bachelor's degree in a relevant field such as computer science, design, human-computer interaction or business, or equivalent experience.

Pinterest is uniquely positioned across the full consumer journey—from inspiration and discovery through consideration, planning, and action. Creators bring ideas to life, Pinners signal emerging interests and intent, and advertisers help people act on what inspires them.

This role will define how Pinterest measures that flywheel, helping advertisers understand how Pinterest and its creators build awareness and drive business outcomes, while helping creators understand the value they generate and unlock new opportunities with brands.
The ideal candidate is a Staff-level product leader with substantial ads measurement experience and a deep understanding of how advertisers set objectives, deploy tactics across the full funnel, and evaluate outcomes. They have worked cross-functionally with engineering, data science, research, PMM, sales, and other partners and can translate complex measurement methods into credible, useful, and scalable products.

Own the strategy and end-to-end execution for demonstrating the full-funnel value of Pinterest, including the creator–Pinner–advertiser flywheel. Define the vision for new and existing measurement capabilities and translate advertiser and creator needs into clear product and technical requirements.

Create and deliver a multi-quarter roadmap, aligning data foundations, measurement methodologies, experimentation, privacy guardrails, and customer-facing experiences to drive measurable creator, advertiser, and Pinner outcomes.
Partner day-to-day with engineering, data science/analytics, design, and research to deliver high-quality products; collaborate with PMM, sales, partnerships, legal, privacy, and policy/integrity for launches. Work closely with PM peers across Ads, Creators, Content, and Shopping to manage dependencies, align measurement frameworks and experiment design, coordinate GTM, and incorporate customer feedback.
Build new and iterate on measurement products that help advertisers understand how creator content, organic engagement, and paid media contribute across awareness, consideration, intent, conversion, and longer-term value. Enable creators to understand the value they generate for brands and identify new business opportunities. Define success metrics and validation standards up front, track adoption and quality post-launch, and use insights to update the roadmap.

8+ years of experience working as a Product Manager or in a related role, including 3–5+ years of substantial ads or marketing measurement experience.

Preferred but not required: Technical degree in CS/Statistics/Math/Engineering/Economics.

Reddit is a community of communities. It’s built on shared interests, passion, and trust, and is home to the most open and authentic conversations on the internet. Every day, Reddit users submit, vote, and comment on the topics they care most about. With 100,000+ active communities and approximately 130 million daily active unique visitors, Reddit is one of the internet’s largest sources of information. For more information, visit www.redditinc.com .

Reddit's developer ecosystem is one of the biggest opportunities to make Reddit more useful, expressive, extensible, and valuable. Today, most people who build on Reddit are developers: they write code, use Devvit, work with APIs, and ship apps or games through a relatively technical workflow. That ecosystem is growing quickly and remains critical.
But the future is bigger than developers alone. AI-assisted building is changing who can create software. The next generation of Reddit apps, games, tools, community agents, content formats, and workflows should be buildable by many more people: developers, technically curious creators, moderators, community builders, game designers, data partners, and eventually people who can describe what they want without needing to code it by hand.
The Developer Ecosystem team owns the product systems that help this broader set of builders discover opportunities, create successfully, launch high-quality apps and games, reach the right users and communities, adopt new platform capabilities, and keep improving after launch.

This includes surfaces and systems like developers.reddit.com, AI-assisted creation, app review, developer and creator onboarding, app marketplace experiences, platform capabilities, best practices, and support for emerging creator categories.

We are looking for a Staff Product Manager to lead Reddit's Builder Ecosystem product strategy. This person will define the roadmap for how Reddit moves from a developer-only ecosystem to a broader builder ecosystem where AI-assisted and no-code creation become first-class parts of the platform.
The role spans developer growth, creator onboarding, AI-assisted building, app quality, ecosystem incentives, platform capabilities, app marketplace strategy, operational tooling, feature adoption, and new builder categories.
This is a high-ambiguity platform role with direct business, product, and community impact. The right PM will be able to bridge two worlds: they should understand the needs of serious developers and platform engineers, while also having strong conviction that Reddit can unlock a much larger wave of builders by making creation more accessible, guided, AI-native, and outcome-oriented.

Define the product strategy for Reddit's Developer Ecosystem, including the transition from code-first developers to a broader base of AI-assisted creators.
Own the roadmap for developers.reddit.com as the primary builder portal, including onboarding, docs, app management, analytics, review status, feature access, education, examples, templates, and AI-assisted creation entry points.
Lead strategy for AI-assisted app creation, including prompt-to-app workflows, AI building tools, no-code or low-code experiences, reusable templates, generated scaffolds, and systems that help creators turn ideas into useful Reddit-native apps.
Build the product approach for an App Marketplace that helps users, moderators, communities, and internal teams discover high-quality apps, games, agents, tools, and community experiences.
Improve app review and ecosystem operations through tooling, automation, and AI-assisted workflows, including LLM-powered app review, policy checks, quality signals, and reviewer efficiency.
Partner with Engineering to prioritize core platform capabilities and performance improvements such as webhooks, webviews, APIs, SDKs, tooling, observability, and other primitives builders need to create reliable apps.
Drive more successful, retentive, and popular apps and games by identifying best practices, improving templates, shaping incentives, and creating clearer paths from idea to launch to growth.
Identify and support new creator and developer categories
Partner with internal teams such as Contribution, Community Builders, Games, Search, Recommendations, Safety, and Ads to help them launch new functionality through the developer ecosystem.
Define and improve feature adoption programs so builders understand, test, and successfully use new platform capabilities.
Work with developer relations to establish the measurement system for the ecosystem, including weekly active developers/creators, NPS/CSAT, app launches, app retention and more
Create clear frameworks for when Reddit should build platform primitives, launch templates, fund builders, partner with external teams, promote apps, or shut down low-quality or low-trust ecosystem behavior.
Lead cross-functional alignment across Product, Engineering, DevRel, Community, Data, Safety, Legal, Policy, Support, BD, and senior leadership.

Experience leading high-ambiguity platform, developer ecosystem, creator ecosystem, marketplace, gaming, AI tooling, or developer experience products.
Strong product judgment for creation platforms: understanding what makes a platform powerful for advanced developers, approachable for new creators, trustworthy for communities, and worth sustained investment.
Comfort with code, APIs, developer tools, technical platform tradeoffs, and engineering conversations, paired with strong conviction that AI-assisted and no-code creation will expand who can build on Reddit.
Ability to reason across multiple sides of the ecosystem: developers, creators, users, moderators, communities, internal teams, partners, and Reddit's business priorities.
Experience improving developer or creator onboarding, docs, portals, SDKs, APIs, marketplaces, app review, app distribution, AI creation tools, or app-building workflows.
Strong analytical judgment and comfort defining metrics for ecosystem health, builder productivity, app quality, retention, distribution, and business impact.
Ability to partner deeply with Engineering on platform capabilities, performance, reliability, primitives, observability, and build-vs-buy decisions.
Strong product sense for apps, games, agents, content creation tools, community-native experiences, and the kinds of lightweight software that should exist inside Reddit communities.
Comfort working with AI-assisted creation tools, LLM-based workflows, prompt-to-app systems, or other emerging ways of helping more people build software.
Excellent written communication and decision frameworks that help teams make crisp investment decisions in ambiguous spaces.

Sierra is the leading platform for customer-facing AI agents, working with many of the world's biggest brands — including The GAP, Rocket Mortgage, SoFi, Sutter Health, and SoftBank — to transform how they serve customers and grow their businesses. We are primarily an in-person company based in San Francisco, with growing offices across North America, Europe, and Asia.
We are guided by a set of values that are at the core of our actions and define our culture: Trust, Customer Obsession, Craftsmanship, Intensity, and a commitment to balancing Family along the way. These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do.
Our co-founders are Bret Taylor and Clay Bavor . Bret currently serves as Board Chair of OpenAI. Previously, he was co-CEO of Salesforce (which had acquired the company he founded, Quip) and CTO of Facebook. Bret was also one of Google's earliest product managers and co-creator of Google Maps.

Before founding Sierra, Clay spent 18 years at Google, where he most recently led Google Labs. Earlier, he started and led Google’s AR/VR effort, Project Starline, and Google Lens. Before that, Clay led the product and design teams for Google Workspace.
About the Public Sector team
Sierra recently received FedRAMP High certification, enabling us to bring our industry-leading technology to partners in the US public sector. We’re now building our founding public sector team to redefine the relationship between the government and its citizenry.
Today, our agents already enable citizens to access social services, report fraud, and understand complex government systems. Simultaneously, they empower government officials to better hear the concerns and inquiries of their constituencies.
We are explicitly nonpartisan and committed to empowering public servants to leverage AI to advance their important missions.
In our journey, we are guided by a set of values that are at the core of our actions and define our culture: Trust, Customer Obsession, Craftsmanship, Intensity, and Family. These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do.

Build enterprise-grade AI agents for government institutions: As an Agent Product Manager at Sierra, you will partner directly with our engineers and public sector customers to build and ship AI agents that serve people across high-stakes, mission-critical interactions. These agents will help constituents navigate complex programs, complete important tasks, and get timely, trustworthy support while meeting the security, accessibility, and reliability standards government work demands.
Discover where agents can make the greatest impact: Ground-up discovery is a critical part of the role. Work closely with federal and state institutions to understand their missions, operating constraints, constituent needs, and service-delivery workflows. Identify and prioritize new opportunities for AI agents to improve access, responsiveness, and outcomes.
Engage with customers at every level: Become a trusted advisor to public sector leaders and a hands-on partner to their working teams. Discover and assess requirements, prepare and present demonstrations, navigate technical and operational challenges with customer counterparts, and continuously improve agents to fit each institution’s policies and workflows.
Own outcomes from concept through production: Translate mission goals into a clear product strategy, roadmap, and measurable definition of success. Coordinate across customer stakeholders, engineering, design, research, security, and operations to take agents from initial concept through launch and ongoing iteration.
Shape the platform and public sector roadmap: Your direct work with government institutions will guide the evolution of Sierra’s core platform. Surface unmet needs, prototype new tools and features, and collaborate with research, product, and platform teams to shape the future of AI agent development for the public sector.
Help build Sierra’s public sector business: Partner closely with public sector leadership on market strategy, product investments, and repeatable approaches that allow the team to scale quickly while preserving the trust and craftsmanship our customers expect.
Example projects
These are examples of projects our healthcare team has worked on:
Build agents that help people understand eligibility, apply for benefits, check case status, and navigate complex social-service programs.

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

Anthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We believe powerful AI can compress a century of scientific progress into a decade. Claude Science is a big part of building toward that future.
Claude Science is an AI workbench that gives researchers a single environment for work that today spans dozens of disconnected tools — literature, specialized databases, scientific computing, analysis, and publication-ready outputs.

Claude Science already renders protein structures, genome tracks, and chemical structures natively, and coordinates multi-agent workflows with built-in review for citation and calculation errors — and we're just getting started. Much of this is being built 0→1 right now, in a category no one has defined yet.
We're growing the Claude Science product team.

As a Product Manager on Claude Science, you will own a major area of the roadmap end to end — think expanding into new scientific fields, landing new model capabilities with researchers, or making the workbench ready for enterprise R&D teams — and help shape the overall product direction alongside the rest of the team.

You'll spend real time with researchers in academic labs, biotech and pharma R&D, and research institutes to understand how science actually gets done — from hypothesis to analysis to publication and beyond— and turn what you learn into shipped product.

You'll partner directly with our research teams to make the models better at science, help decide which fields and workflows we go after next, and shape what it takes for Claude Science to be trusted in enterprise and regulated research environments.
We're looking for experienced product managers and founders with real scientific or technical depth: people who can hold their own in a conversation with a structural biologist or a computational chemist, get in the weeds of model transcripts and evals, and still zoom out to help define a product category. You thrive in ambiguity, uncover non-obvious use cases for nascent capabilities, and bring those insights back to research.
Our north star is for Claude Science to accelerate scientific progress — across biology, chemistry, physics, and beyond — from early discovery through real-world application, by an order of magnitude.

What to Expect from the Hiring Process We believe hiring should feel like a conversation, not a test. Here’s what you can expect if you apply: Step 1 — Conversation with People & Culture (30 minutes) If your experience looks like a fit, you’ll meet with our Head of People & Culture for a video chat.

It’s a two-way conversation, we’ll learn about your background, skills, and what energizes you, and you’ll have space to ask about Revaly , our mission, and what it’s like to work here. It’s also a chance to make sure the vibes are right on both sides.

Step 2 — Conversation with the Hiring Manager (60 minutes) Next, you’ll meet with the hiring manager for a deeper dive into your role-specific experience. We’ll talk through real scenarios, how you approach challenges, and what success looks like in this role. You’ll also get a clearer picture of the team’s goals and priorities.

Step 3 — Meet a Future Teammate (60 minutes) In this stage, you’ll meet with someone from the team you’ll work closely with. This is your chance to get an on-the-ground perspective, how the team collaborates, what day-to-day looks like, and the kind of people you’ll be building alongside.

Step 4 — 90 Day Ramp Up Presentation (30 minutes) In this final stage, we ask candidates to prepare and present a 90 day ramp up plan to the hiring manager. This is an opportunity for candidates to outline how they would approach their first 3 months in the role, what they’d aim to learn, prioritize, and accomplish.

This is a chance to show your understanding of the role, the company, and the environment we’re operating in, while giving the hiring manager a glimpse into how you think, structure your approach to learning and communicate your ideas.

We hire for both skill and fit, looking for people who are not just aligned with our values, but who will add to our culture with their ideas, energy, and perspective.

If you’ve applied for a role in Technology or Product Development, you can also expect a skill-based assessment between step 3 and 4, to help us assess some key role-based requirements.

Revaly is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law. Accommodation is available upon request for applicants with disabilities.

Working as a Product Manager at MG AI
While engineers focus on building and shipping models, Product Managers at MG AI own the why and the what. We translate complex, often ambiguous business challenges from Match Group's brands into clear ML product strategy, and we drive execution across a globally distributed team. The PMs who thrive here are strategic troubleshooters with a bias for action: they spot what is blocking progress and drive it to resolution instead of waiting.
This is a communication-first role, but that does not mean coordination alone. Your core job is to figure out which problem is worth solving, articulate it in clear and precise language, and drive alignment among a diverse set of stakeholders across cultures and time zones. You own the product thinking end to end: framing the problem, shaping the plan, and defining what we build.
You will work on projects that leverage a wide range of technologies, from on-device ML modules to server-side AI models and LLMs. You do not need to be an ML expert on day one, but you must learn fast and become technically fluent enough to make sound product calls, because the technology and the problems keep changing.

Frame the Problem: Figure out which problems are worth solving and why, and articulate them in clear, precise language that a diverse team can rally around.
Shape the Roadmap: Decide what matters most, sequence the work, make the tradeoffs, and write PRDs, keeping partners aligned as priorities shift.
Navigate Complex Stakeholder Maps: Act as the connective tissue between Match Group's brands, and the many functions within them, and MG AI engineering. Read the unspoken dynamics, build alignment across brands, functions, cultures, and time zones, and keep everyone moving in the same direction.
Hands-on Execution: Stay deeply involved in the details. Use experiments, behavioral data, and research to guide your calls when signals are imperfect, unblock engineering, and make the small decisions that keep a project moving.

Exceptional Communication & Stakeholder Management (most important): You excel at managing stakeholders in complex, high-ambiguity situations. You read between the lines, sense interpersonal and organizational dynamics, and build alignment across teams with competing priorities. This is the single most important quality for this role.
4-6 years of product management experience in the Tech domain, ideally on complex systems or data or ML-driven products.
Fast Learning Curve & Strong Will to Learn: You do not need to be ML-savvy today, but you must ramp quickly and become technically fluent enough to shape direction on model behavior and tradeoffs without needing to be deeply technical.
Fluent in English (Able to conduct business meetings and participate in complex discussions without requiring assistance.)
Fluent in Korean (Sophisticated professional interactions with native-level precision and an understanding of cultural nuances.) Essential for cross-functional collaboration within the Seoul office.
Strong Ownership & Bias for Action: A track record of driving problems to resolution without waiting for permission. You are comfortable operating with ambiguity and making principled calls when the signals are imperfect.
Analytical Rigor: Comfort with data. You can define metrics, design and read experiments, and let evidence guide your decisions.
Global Operational Readiness: Ability to accommodate flexible working hours for regular early morning syncs with US teams (EST/PST).

A Point of View on AI Tooling: A clear sense of how AI tools can raise the quality and speed of product work, and a habit of using them (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor).
ML Product Experience: Exposure to ML-driven products (Recommendation, Search, Ranking, or Trust & Safety) and a working understanding of the ML lifecycle, from data to online A/B testing.
Matching Products Experience: Experience with products that match people or content (e.g., dating, marketplaces, social feeds, or hiring).
Internal Platform / B2B2C Experience: Success in a role where your primary customers were other internal business units or engineering teams.
Cross-functional Collaboration: Experience working with diverse, globally distributed teams and organizations.

Scale has been the leading AI data foundry, helping fuel the most exciting advancements in AI, including frontier model training, enterprise adoption, defense applications, and autonomous vehicles. Our mission is to develop reliable AI systems for the world's most important decisions.
The next frontier for AI is the physical world. We're looking for an AI Product Manager to own the Robotics vertical within our Physical AI team.

In this role, you'll own both the development of the data and training environments (the teleoperated demonstrations, real-world collections, simulated tasks, and annotation products that labs use to train and evaluate robot policies) and the "data as a product" strategy that powers them.

You'll understand where physical AI is headed, decide what robot tasks and embodiments are worth collecting, how to source and structure the underlying data, and how to turn deep domain knowledge into a defensible product.
The ideal candidate has lived inside robotics or physical AI research, and is able to pair that domain understanding with a sense for where current robot policies succeed and fail in real-world workflows.
You'll translate that expertise into datasets, environments, and evaluation frameworks that teach robots to do real physical work, and you'll be the domain expert Scale's most important customers and their leading researchers turn to. A strong entrepreneurial & go-to-market mindset will be necessary.

Own the Robotics AI roadmap & data strategy: Set product direction for the robotics training stack and the data strategy behind it — what data we collect, on which hardware and embodiments, and what we source internally vs. through our marketplace. Establish a vision for where physical AI is heading, driving execution across engineering, operations, and go-to-market teams.
Build partnerships with research teams at frontier labs: Work directly with researchers at leading physical AI labs to understand where their robot policies fall short and shape new product lines and competitive strategy for the vertical. Connect with robotics startups and industry leaders to launch joint benchmarks and build Scale's brand in physical AI.
Design and scale robotics data products and environments: Scope and deliver high-quality collection pipelines, annotation tooling, simulated tasks, and evaluation frameworks — spanning robot-based collection (humanoids and robotic arms performing real-world tasks) and robot-less collection (wearable cameras capturing human demonstrations). Partner with ML and Operations to translate research needs into training products that hit quality, throughput, and cost targets.
Collaborate cross-functionally — influence business priorities and dive into the weeds of research, operations, and customer interactions to deliver mission-critical outcomes. Travel ~10–15% to meet customers, attend conferences, and visit our global data operations.

About the opportunity
Conversational Banking is how N26 scales support without scaling headcount at the same rate. Our ambition is banking as a non event: clients get help in their channel and language of choice, and most issues resolve before a human agent ever needs to be involved. We build the intelligence in house — N26 owns its own orchestration and intelligence layer rather than renting it from vendors — and the programme is now shifting from an assistant that answers questions to a system that acts on them.
As Product Manager, you will own one of the highest value capability areas within the programme end to end — from discovery through delivery to measured resolution outcomes. You will work at the intersection of applied AI, banking operations and regulation, shipping capabilities that millions of clients across Europe use without thinking about them. That is the point.
The segment has been newly formed and expanded, the platform foundations are proven, and the interesting work is just starting: taking journeys from containment to genuine autonomous resolution, on infrastructure the bank owns. You will join a small senior team with direct access to the programme's leadership and real ownership from day one.
In this role, you will
Own a capability area. Take full product ownership of a defined slice of the programme — for example a set of high volume client journeys or an agent facing capability — including its roadmap, delivery and outcomes.
Ground everything in evidence. Lead discovery on the contact drivers behind your area, building problem statements from real client voice and operational data rather than assumption.
Ship agentic capabilities. Work daily with engineering and applied AI teams to move journeys from answering to acting — safe, autonomous resolution with the right guardrails and escalation paths.
Own your numbers. Instrument your area with resolution first metrics and the counter metrics that prove quality isn't traded for efficiency. You should be able to defend every figure you present.
Work the interfaces. Collaborate with operations, service partners and peer product teams so that what you ship lands in the real workflows of agents and back office teams.
Build for a regulated bank. Design compliance, auditability and client protection into every capability from the start.

Three or more years in product management, with at least one shipped product or major capability you owned end to end.
Experience with AI powered, conversational or automation products — or a demonstrable, hands on understanding of how LLM based systems behave in production.
Strong analytical fluency, comfortable defining metrics, working directly with data, and separating signal from vanity.
Bias to evidence over opinion, and comfort operating with ambiguity in a fast moving programme.

Experience in banking, fintech or another regulated industry.
Exposure to contact centre and branch operations, BPO environments or customer service tooling.

Accelerate your career growth by leading core infrastructure at one of Europe’s premier digital banks.
Employee benefits including a competitive personal development budget, work from home budget, fitness & wellness discounts, and public transportation subsidies.
A Premium N26 bank account subscription for you, plus subscriptions for friends and family.
An additional day of annual leave for each year of service.
High autonomy to drive the ML technical agenda, working with a diverse, international team of peers.

N26 has reimagined banking for today’s digital world. Technology and design empower everything we do and it’s how we are building the global banking platform the world loves to use.
We've eliminated physical branches, paperwork, and hidden fees for an elegant digital experience and supreme savings. Giving people the power to live and bank their way is what gets us out of bed in the morning and inspires the work that we do.

You know version control is more than just a subsystem. It’s the backbone of how teams build software. You’re ready to shape the future of code-change workflows, from local commits to AI-assisted reviews. If you’re excited by the challenge of turning a core IDE feature into a standalone ecosystem, this is for you.

About JetBrains

We create intelligent software development tools for developers and teams. More than 15 million users, over 300,000 companies, and 88 of the Fortune Global Top 100 rely on our products to solve real, complex problems. Our mission is simple: make development teams more productive and AI adoptable at scale.

Version control is a critical part of our IDEs, but we want to take it further. We’re turning VCS into a strategic product direction and, eventually, we aim to grow it into a dedicated ecosystem. This role exists to define what that future looks like right now.

As the Senior Product Manager, you’ll figure out where JetBrains should play in the VCS space, how to evolve our Git and code review experiences, and what new opportunities exist beyond our current tools.

You’ll have the ownership to set a clear product vision that covers everything from complex local merges to remote, containerized, and AI-assisted workflows. You’ll collaborate closely with engineering and quality leads, as well as product marketing, developer advocacy, and the IntelliJ Platform teams.

Together, you'll figure out how to handle the next era of software delivery, including tracking provenance and reviewing AI-generated changes across different environments.

· Set the long-term product strategy for VCS and code-change workflows across all JetBrains IDEs.

· Identify gaps in current developer workflows and define new product directions in the VCS space.

· Explore new opportunities, from cross-IDE VCS clients and host-neutral code reviews to AI-native review and authorship tracking.

· Listen closely to what the community and the industry are saying to figure out exactly what we should be working on.

· Align roadmap decisions across the product, engineering, design, marketing, developer advocacy, partnership, and customer-facing teams.

· Work with engineering and quality leads to balance user value, technical constraints, and platform health.

· Shape external positioning and represent our VCS direction in conversations with customers and the broader developer tools community.

· A collaborative mindset that works well with engineering and quality teams on deeply technical challenges.

· Strong product judgment, especially when navigating ambiguous areas to define a new ecosystem.

· The ability to think beyond existing boundaries and spot opportunities for entirely new workflows.

· Clear communication skills, whether you’re aligning internal stakeholders or talking to deeply technical users.

· A data-informed approach, combining usage metrics, customer feedback, and market signals to make decisions.

· An interest in how AI is changing software development, from generated commits to AI-assisted reviews.

· A drive to improve solutions instead of copying what already exists.

What you’ll need

· Previous success leading the product direction and strategy for technically complex developer tools, SCM, CI/CD, or code collaboration software.

· The proven ability to translate intricate developer workflows into clear product roadmaps.

· Experience bringing stakeholders together across product, engineering, marketing, and developer advocacy.

· A deep understanding of version control mechanics, code-change workflows, and how developers actually ship code.

· Based in the EU, ideally Munich, Prague, Amsterdam, Berlin, Belgrade, or remote within the EU, with the ability to travel to JetBrains offices as needed.

· As a plus, familiarity with advanced version control scenarios, such as complex merges, monorepos, and enterprise/self-hosted setups.

What success looks like

Success means moving VCS from a platform subsystem to a clear, strategic ecosystem. You’ll have built a compelling product vision that engineering teams are aligned on and customers are excited about. You won’t just be copying what exists.

You’ll be finding entirely new ways to solve code-change workflows, especially as AI becomes a bigger part of development. Ultimately, you’ll earn your team's trust by making sound decisions, keeping projects moving, and leaving the product better than you found it.

As a Technical Product Manager, you’ll own a product vertical end to end—such as payments and expense management, remittance, insurance, or wealth and trading—from strategy, outcomes, and roadmap through to the technical design and delivery of the systems behind it.

This is a product where real money moves, mistakes are immediately visible, and licensing, compliance, and third-party rails are core product constraints—not considerations around the edges. We are AI-native by default, but AI is a means, not the goal.

The bar is knowing where a model can genuinely improve an outcome, where deterministic systems must remain in control, and how to build products that are reliable, auditable, and trusted when money is involved. What you'll be doing
Own a vertical end-to-end — outcomes and metrics, a backlog prioritised by value / risk / dependency / strategic priority, acceptance criteria crisp enough to build and test against.
Shape the technical design with engineering — system boundaries, money-movement correctness (idempotency, ledgering, reconciliation), third-party-rail reliance and rail-down behaviour, failure/retry/refund paths, security, latency, scalability, recovery.
Make hard trade-offs across correctness, speed, cost, reliability and UX — and defend them to an engineering, compliance or ops lead who pushes back.
Treat regulated constraints as first-class product inputs — licensing scope, CDD/KYC and limits, sanctions/PEP screening, transaction monitoring, data residency and privacy. Know which are hard launch gates and which are forward-readiness.
Apply AI where it earns its place — define what it's allowed to decide, where a human stays in the loop, how it's evaluated, and what it does when unsure. Every AI-surfaced number traces back to a real record.
Ship against external gates — build feature-complete behind flags; go live per rail as each partner and regulatory gate clears.
Work across Engineering, Design, Compliance, Operations, Treasury and Finance/Reconciliation.
What you'll need
Product leadership — significant experience owning a complex technical product end-to-end; strong judgement and decisiveness under ambiguity; ability to balance ambition against technical, regulatory and operational reality; can hold their own with senior engineers.
Technical foundation — solid system design (boundaries, datastores, queues/workflows, APIs, failure modes, consistency under concurrency); comfort reading, reviewing and challenging design docs; can sketch an architecture and a sequence. No production code, but technical enough that engineers don't have to simplify.
Domain — experience in a regulated / high-consequence domain (payments, banking, remittance, insurance, …) or demonstrable fast-ramp ability; understands why money movement is different (correctness over convenience, irreversible states, partners you don't control).
AI judgement — hands-on with LLM-based products; can frame a feature as eval-able (offline, online, human feedback); realistic on hallucination/drift/data gaps, including data-blocked vs model-blocked and when a model must not be in the loop at all.
Nice to have — engineer or highly-technical-PM background · zero-to-one · shipped AI-heavy consumer products · defined eval metrics for ML/LLM systems · AI UX + failure-handling intuition · SEA market experience.
Outcomes
Clear vertical strategy and legible roadmap
Ships fast and clears the gates that actually block launch
Money is correct and users are never misled about the state of their funds
AI features are valuable, predictable and trusted
Trade-offs made deliberately under uncertainty and hold up when challenged
Engineering, design, compliance, and operations are aligned with minimal friction

Location
This role is remote, but candidates must be based in Philippines . We are hiring specifically for this market, so applicants should already be based in Philippines . Language English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required. Interview Process Our process is designed to move fast: 1.

Online assessment or practical task 2. Role-specific interview 3. CEO / final round For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Apply AI where it earns its place — define what it's allowed to decide, where a human stays in the loop, how it's evaluated, and what it does when unsure. Every AI-surfaced number traces back to a real record.
Ship against external gates — build feature-complete behind flags; go live per rail as each partner and regulatory gate clears.
Work across Engineering, Design, Compliance, Operations, Treasury and Finance/Reconciliation.
What you'll need
Product leadership — significant experience owning a complex technical product end-to-end; strong judgement and decisiveness under ambiguity; ability to balance ambition against technical, regulatory and operational reality; can hold their own with senior engineers.
Technical foundation — solid system design (boundaries, datastores, queues/workflows, APIs, failure modes, consistency under concurrency); comfort reading, reviewing and challenging design docs; can sketch an architecture and a sequence. No production code, but technical enough that engineers don't have to simplify.
Domain — experience in a regulated / high-consequence domain (payments, banking, remittance, insurance, …) or demonstrable fast-ramp ability; understands why money movement is different (correctness over convenience, irreversible states, partners you don't control).

Nice to have — engineer or highly-technical-PM background · zero-to-one · shipped AI-heavy consumer products · defined eval metrics for ML/LLM systems · AI UX + failure-handling intuition · SEA market experience.

Clear vertical strategy and legible roadmap
Ships fast and clears the gates that actually block launch
Money is correct and users are never misled about the state of their funds
AI features are valuable, predictable and trusted
Trade-offs made deliberately under uncertainty and hold up when challenged
Engineering, design, compliance, and operations are aligned with minimal friction

This is a fully remote position and we're considering candidates in Canada EST. About Product Management: As a Product Manager at Grafana Labs , you'll develop a vision and strategy for your product domain.

You will own your product’s roadmap, collateral, and market research, and you will collaborate with Grafana leadership on fine-tuning your product’s goals. You will be the primary advocate and expert in your area, with a strong ability to communicate needs, functionality, and details effectively both to external customers and internal stakeholders.

The teams and people you will be interacting with will be 100% remote and globally distributed, so strong and proactive communication is essential. Product Managers are the bridge that connect Engineering, Design, and UX to GTM.

You are a facilitator who ensures the free flow of information across these teams and are expected to be technically proficient when representing our products to our customers.

As the Senior Product Manager for Infrastructure Observability (Infra O11y) you’ll be responsible for our most popular Grafana Cloud products that span the infrastructure suite: Kubernetes Monitoring and Cloud Provider Observability. Infra O11y provides our customers with the ability to easily monitor their core services – from our smallest self-serve customers to our largest enterprise customers.
Your primary responsibility will be to help define the vision and ensure the long-term success of Infra O11y, working with your engineering partners to fine-tune product strategy. You will be charting the path forward for net-new product initiatives – like Host Monitoring – balanced with maintaining a strong roadmap and customer satisfaction for our most mature products.
Your role will require heavy customer discovery, understanding user needs, and building consensus and alignment across several Engineering groups and many stakeholders as we look towards simplifying our broader Infra O11y experience for Grafana Cloud. You will also need to flex your GTM muscles and build conviction in areas like competitive analysis and sales enablement to better inform activities like pricing and packaging.
Beyond driving your individual product area, you’ll also need to ensure that the experiences you’re building are tightly woven into our overall Grafana Cloud suite of products, by establishing integration touchpoints with other key offerings like Grafana Cloud Knowledge Graph and Grafana Assistant, so that our customers have a seamless monitoring experience where they can easily navigate between different layers of their architecture through guided explorations and natural language.

Transform ideas and feedback into a product vision and roadmap
Empathize with customer problems in order to collect user needs, requirements, and pain points
Curate and properly represent user feedback to Engineering, while providing evidence to support tradeoffs and priorities
Work closely with PMM to enable GTM on product differentiation, including creating and updating presentations, documentation, website content, datasheets, and whitepapers.
Use your deep product expertise to make decisions about our go-to-market strategies, pricing, packaging, licensing and tiering

Location Our Technical Product Owner - DoiT Cloud Intelligence - Core Services will be an integral part of our global Product team. This role is based remotely in the East Coast US, the UK, Ireland, Estonia, the Netherlands, Sweden and Israel.

Who We Are DoiT is a global technology company that works with cloud-driven organizations to leverage the cloud to drive business growth and innovation. We combine data, technology, and human expertise to ensure our customers operate in a well-architected and scalable state - from planning to production.

Delivering DoiT Cloud Intelligence, the only solution that integrates advanced technology with human intelligence, we help our customers solve complex multi-cloud problems and drive efficiency. With decades of multi-cloud experience, we have specializations in Kubernetes, GenAI, CloudOps, and more.

An award-winning strategic partner of AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure, we work alongside more than 4,000 customers worldwide.

The Opportunity We’re hiring a Technical Product Owner to drive rapid delivery and iteration for the Core Services team of DoiT Cloud Intelligence, our platform that helps DevOps, Cloud Infrastructure, and FinOps teams manage public cloud environments effectively and efficiently.

Core Services builds and operates foundational platform capabilities used across DoiT’s products and engineering teams. Its responsibilities include identity and access management, authentication and authorization, customer and tenant services, shared APIs, platform integrations, and other cross-cutting capabilities.

This role is designed for someone with a technical product mindset who is comfortable working deep within platform architecture, distributed systems, APIs, cloud infrastructure, and internal engineering workflows.

You will help turn broad platform needs into clear technical product direction, sequenced investments, and reliably delivered capabilities. You will report to a VP of Product and work as an embedded member of the Core Services Engineering team.

You will collaborate closely with engineering leadership, architects, security, product teams, and internal platform consumers to determine what the team should build next and why. Role clarity: VP of Product vs. Technical Product Owner VP of Product (what they own)
Sets the overall vision, strategy, positioning, and long-range roadmap for the platform area.
Makes the highest-level prioritization calls across multiple components and investment themes.
Aligns stakeholders across the company (executive leadership, GTM, partners) on direction and tradeoffs.
Defines success at the portfolio/area level and ensures the area’s outcomes ladder up to company goals.
Technical Product Owner (what you own)
Owns delivery, iteration, and learning velocity for the Core Services.
Turns VP-level direction into clear problems to solve, a prioritized backlog, and incrementally shippable scope.
Runs the feedback loop: discover → define → build → release → measure → iterate, repeatedly.
Works within the Engineering teams to ensure they are always building the highest-value next increment with clarity, quality
Review technical designs, reason about tradeoffs and constraints, and understand their impact on delivery timelines and system behavior, without being the primary implementer
Leverages deep, hands-on DevOps experience and public cloud understanding to ensure that solution implementations are done correctly
This distinction matters: the VP creates the “why” and “where”; the Product Owner ensures the “what next” is always sharp, validated, and shipping. Responsibilities Fast iteration and backlog leadership
Translate the VP’s strategy into a sequenced backlog of problems, user stories, and acceptance criteria that the Engineering team can deliver continuously.
Keep work “thin-sliced” so the team can ship frequently, learn quickly, and reduce risk through iteration.
Maintain a disciplined cadence of backlog refinement, sprint readiness, and scope negotiation to keep delivery predictable without slowing innovation.
Deep user and workflow understanding
Leverage your hands-on DevOps experience and expertise in the real-world workflows of the professionals you’re building for - especially cloud operators and practitioners.
Use firsthand domain knowledge and ongoing customer conversations to identify friction, gaps, and opportunities for differentiation.
Prioritize enhancements that materially improve outcomes: speed, reliability, clarity, safety, governance, cost impact, or operational simplicity.
Customer validation and external communication
Often speak with customers (aiming for 3-5 calls a week) and cross-functional DoiT stakeholders regularly to test ideas, validate assumptions, and pressure-test tradeoffs.
Communicate clearly and confidently: share concepts early, take feedback openly, synthesize input into decisions, and explain “why” in a way that builds trust.
Rely on your hands-on, DevOps experience to go deep with stakeholders (internal/external) into the technical details of the problem, our solution, and the contexts and environments in which both of these exist.
Support beta/design-partner motions where appropriate by shaping hypotheses, success criteria, and rollout plans.
Engineering-embedded technical product ownership
Operate as a core member of the Core Services’ Engineering team - present in daily collaboration, crisp in decision-making, and pragmatic about constraints.
Partner with Engineering leads on sequencing, technical tradeoffs, and delivery planning - ensuring product intent survives implementation realities.
Ensure Core Services are cohesive across UX, APIs, data, and operational behavior - and that it meets a high bar for reliability and customer trust.
Quality, outcomes, and measurement
Define what “success” means for Core Services with clear metrics (adoption, activation, workflow completion, time-to-value, retention, reliability signals, customer-reported impact).
Instrument learning: make sure releases are measurable and that insights reliably flow back into prioritization.
Own release readiness for Core Services: documentation, enablement inputs, and clear communication of what’s new and why it matters.
Safety, governance, and trust by design
Ensure product requirements account for real-world cloud environments: IAM boundaries, auditability, guardrails, and safe defaults.
Partner with security, support, and customer teams to anticipate edge cases and ensure Core Services earns trust over time.

7–10 years of hands-on experience as a Platform Engineer, DevOps Engineer, SRE, Cloud Engineer, Solutions Architect, or a similar roles working with or building products for public cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, and/or Azure).
A strong product sense for turning messy problems into clear scope and shipped value - without waiting for perfect information.
Systems thinking: Ability to reason about complex distributed systems, architectural tradeoffs, and long-term platform evolution.
Prioritization: Demonstrated ability to balance customer needs, engineering constraints, and platform investments when making prioritization decisions.

Imagine the what. Build the how.

Your opportunity

You'll work at the intersection of UX, mobile engineering, and computer vision to make capture fast, simple, and reliable, and to ensure the right shelf data is collected at the right quality, coverage, and cost.

ShelfView turns images and video from mobile devices, fixed cameras, and autonomous robots into a digital twin of the store, generating insights that remove tedious tasks for retail workers. Your mission is to make the capture experience best-in-class for accuracy, cost, and speed.

· Partner with customers and field teams to understand capture environments and translate needs into requirements.

· Build and drive the ShelfView capture roadmap toward high throughput, coverage, and quality at the right cost.

· Define and deliver a better capture experience (e.g., improved video capture, AR guidance, faster and more reliable first-time-right capture).

· Own how capture work is tasked and scheduled — which stores and aisles are captured, how often, and by whom.

· Own store onboarding and modeling — getting stores ready (mapping, planograms, catalogs) and keeping them current as stores change.

· Define capture quality, product metrics, and telemetry , and run experiments to inform iterative development.

· Work closely with design, mobile engineering, and CV teams to evaluate new technologies that improve capture success

· Drive non-mobile, hybrid capture (fixed camera, robot and emerging technologies).

· Coordinate feature launches with product marketing and sales operations; act as the capture point of contact on pilots and early customer rollouts.

· Degree in Engineering or a related field.

· 6+ years of product management experience in a "Deep Tech" or mobile SaaS company, or equivalent product leadership experience in a startup.

· Experience with mobile apps, AR use-cases, or on-device ML is beneficial.

· Strong problem-solving and analytical skills to identify user needs; comfortable working hands-on with data/telemetry.

· Open-minded, sociable, and driven personality.

· Excellent English communication skills, both written and oral.

· Eligible to work in Switzerland.

· Ability to visit customers in Europe and North America on occasion.

· You will either be living within a commutable distance of our Zurich office.

Liberis is in the middle of a meaningful shift. We started as a single-product business and are quickly becoming a truly multi-product embedded finance company, with different funding structures, revenue models and customer relationships sitting alongside each other in the same portfolio. That complexity creates real demand for better data, better insight and clearer thinking about how all of it fits together - with this role sitting at the centre of that challange!

As our Senior Data Product Manager, you’ll sit right at the intersection of product, analytics, engineering and senior leadership, helping define the data products that power smarter decisions across Liberis.

You’ll have real ownership over roadmap, prioritisation and ways of working, and your work will directly influence how teams access, understand and use data day to day. This role is a high-impact opportunity for someone who wants to shape how a business uses data at scale!

You’ll be joining a team with a broad remit and a genuine mandate to improve the data experience across the company, so there’s a lot of scope to make the role your own and shape the future of the domain.

You will own the data and insights product for Liberis, building the foundations that let our commercial, credit and operations teams actually understand the business they're running.

That means, thinking carefully about the entities in our data model, how products and customers relate to each other, how those relationships surface in reporting and analysis - and how it eventually all comes out in great dashboards, tools and self-serve capabilities.

This is about shipping products which are genuinely useful, not just technically correct.

Our Engineering Team is going through an AI-first transformation, rethinking how teams are structured and how they ship. Data, insights and analytics are a crucial part of that journey and you will be a key player in leading, innovating and rapidly improving our posture and capabilities at the intersection of data and AI.

If you like solving genuinely hard problems, bringing clarity to complex environments and building products that have visible business impact - this is the role for you!

Your primary job is to help Liberis's commercial decision makers understand the small businesses we serve and how they consider, use and perform across our product range. Doing this well requires a clear conceptual model of the business and a willingness to engage with stakeholders across the business, as well as taste and customer empathy in developing a great insights product including dashboards, insight tools and self-serve capabilities.

You will own the roadmap for our internal data & insight products. Working with stakeholders across commercial, credit, finance and operations, you will define what good looks like and then work with your team to build it. You will run prioritisation, manage the backlog and make decisions about where effort goes.

You will also spend a meaningful amount of time in the detail, reviewing data models and dashboards, asking hard questions about definitions, and making sure what we ship is accurate and trusted.

You will partner closely with the engineering side of your team on how data is modelled and structured in BigQuery and DBT, and with analysts on how it gets presented in Looker. You don't need to write production code, but you need enough technical understanding to be a genuine partner in those conversations. You will also be responsible for continuing to expand our partner-facing reporting, whereby partners gain visibility into their portfolio.

This role requires someone who can think clearly about complex data structures and translate that thinking into products that non-technical people actually find useful. The ideal person has strong conceptual thinking skills, great product instincts and enough technical depth to earn the trust of the engineers and analysts they work with.

· Proven experience in a senior data product or analytics product role in a business with real complexity

· A track record of helping commercial teams make better decisions through better data, not just shipping dashboards

· Strong ability to think about entities, taxonomies and relationships in data

· Hands-on experience with Looker and LookML and familiarity with best practices and scalable approaches to these systems

· Working knowledge of SQL, DBT and BigQuery, enough to engage seriously with how data is modelled and what's feasible, and to express your thinking in code-speak where needed

· Experience working with a multi skilled team of analysts and data engineers

· Clear, confident communication with senior commercial stakeholders

Next steps If this opportunity feels like the right fit for your next career move, we’d love to hear from you!

Even if you don’t meet every requirement, don’t hesitate to apply or reach out to Chess (Internal Recruiter) on

Our hybrid approach

Working together in person helps us move faster, collaborate better, and build a great Liberis culture. Our hybrid working policy requires team members to be in the office at least 3 days a week, but ideally 4 days. At Liberis, we embrace flexibility as a core part of our culture, while also valuing the importance of the time our teams spend together in the office.

About ScholarshipOwl
ScholarshipOwl is the largest scholarship marketplace in the U.S., connecting over 14 million Gen Z students with private scholarships — and the brands that power them. Our mission is to make education financing more accessible and engaging, while giving brands a way to connect with the next generation.
We’re powered by AI technology that simplifies scholarship discovery, streamlines the application process, and delivers measurable results for both students and partners. Whether it’s helping students secure funding or enabling brands to run impactful campaigns, we’re reshaping how education is funded — and discovered.

We’re looking for a Growth Product Manager to take full ownership of the conversion engine at ScholarshipOwl, from the first visitor touchpoint through to a paid subscription. This is a high-impact, high-velocity role for someone who lives in the data, thrives on experimentation, and values action over perfection.
You will be the architect of our growth. You’ll spend your days identifying leaks in the funnel, hypothesizing solutions, and working alongside a dedicated pod of engineers and designers to ship experiments that move the needle on revenue and retention. If you are a "full-stack" growth thinker who can move from a Mixpanel cohort analysis to a detailed technical spec this is the role for you.

Own the Conversion Engine: Take end-to-end responsibility for the user journey, optimizing every step from landing page registration to paywall conversion and subscription retention.
Drive the Experiment Roadmap: Build, prioritize, and maintain a high-tempo experimentation backlog. You will use frameworks (like ICE or RICE) to ensure we are always working on the highest-leverage growth bets.
Analyze & Diagnose: Monitor funnel and retention metrics daily in Mixpanel. You’ll identify exactly where users are dropping off and perform deep-dive discovery to understand the why .
Ship with Velocity: Write precise product specs and acceptance criteria that allow engineering and design to execute independently. We prioritize shipping "good enough" tests today to get data, rather than waiting for "perfect" features next month.
Optimize Revenue Levers: Design and run pricing, paywall, and offer optimization tests. You’ll also evaluate new growth levers like organic loops, landing page personalization, and winback programs.
Collaborate Cross-Functionally: Lead a dedicated pod of engineers and designers, maintaining strong working relationships with our dashboard and B2B teams to drive unified sprint priorities.
Continuous Discovery: Conduct meaningful customer discovery interviews with our Gen-Z audience to uncover behavioral insights that data alone can’t show.

4+ years of Product Management experience , specifically in a **Growth-**focused role.
Experimentation Mastery: Proven track record of designing, running, and analyzing A/B tests that resulted in measurable improvements to business KPIs (CVR, ARPU, Churn).
Data Fluency: You are a power user of product analytics tools (Mixpanel, Amplitude, or similar). You don't wait for a data analyst; you find the answers yourself.
SaaS/Subscription Expertise: You understand the nuances of subscription models—trial-to-paid transitions, renewal cycles, and friction-point reduction.
Technical Precision: Ability to write clear, "dev-ready" product specs and acceptance criteria. You understand technical trade-offs and how to scope an MVP.
Mentoring & Leadership: A mentoring and knowledge-sharing mindset with a desire to level up the broader team on growth methodologies and experimentation rigor.
Gen-Z Empathy: You have an intuition for (or experience with) B2C products targeting younger audiences and understand their unique digital behaviors.
Growth Mindset: You are comfortable with ambiguity, fast-moving environments, and the fact that 70% of experiments might fail—as long as we learn from them.

Experience with payment platforms (Stripe, Braintree) or Figma/prototyping tools.
Knowledge of lifecycle/email marketing , SEO , and paid acquisition channels.
Growth-focused certifications (e.g., Reforge).
Background in EdTech or student-facing products.
