Semarchy has grown into an industry leader in the data management space. We're searching for a Product Manager to help expand the Semarchy Data Platform (SDP) and support our development teams. As a Product Manager, you are one of our core creative talents.

Reporting to the Head of Product Management and working closely with engineering, design, and the field, you will turn customer problems and market evidence into product capabilities that customers value — and pay for. Your goal will be to increase the adoption and market fit of the Semarchy Data Platform.

You will own your product scope end-to-end: discovering what customers actually need, framing the problems worth solving, prioritizing ruthlessly, shaping the roadmap, and partnering across teams to bring capabilities to market successfully.

Your early focus is likely to involve Semarchy 's AI-oriented capabilities — such as agentic access to governed Data Products and AI-assisted stewardship — so experience or genuine enthusiasm in this area is a real advantage.

As with any growing product organization, scope and responsibilities will be shaped together and are expected to evolve over time. We are therefore looking for someone adaptable and curious, who thrives when the problem space is still taking shape. Responsibilities
Discovery & customer research: Run structured problem discovery — investigate problem spaces, validate pain intensity and business impact, map current alternatives, and confirm willingness to change. Engage continuously with customers and partners, including active participation in design partner programs.
Focus on customer value: Anchor every decision in customer outcomes rather than mechanisms. Be able to articulate the customer, the problem, and why it matters — and bring that evidence into product decisions.
Roadmapping & prioritization: Own and maintain the roadmap for your area with regular reviews, clear milestones, and transparent change rationale. Prioritize using evidence rather than assumption, make deliberate trade-offs, and contribute to a monthly-updated, prioritized roadmap that reflects what the market actually needs.
Delivery: Partner closely with engineering and design through the full product delivery lifecycle, from discovery to release. Produce specifications and UI concepts, and refine and organize the product backlog — shaping the end-to-end experience, not just features.
Commercialization & field enablement: Play a key role in the commercialization process, coordinating the activities within your scope — such as internal training, previews, enablement, and messaging — so releases reach customers fully field-ready. Contribute captivating documentation and customer-facing assets (blogs, whitepapers, solution briefs) that help the field and marketing communicate value, and participate in commercialization retrospectives.
AI-oriented capabilities (initial focus): Shape how customers connect their enterprise AI ecosystem to governed, trusted data (e.g., agentic / MCP-based access). Explore and validate AI-assisted stewardship and governed AI participation, and help translate fast-moving AI research and prototypes into shippable, differentiated value.
Evangelism: Champion Semarchy products to internal and external audiences — talking to customers, partners, industry analysts, and field personnel — and feed their input back into product strategy and prioritization.

Proven experience as a product manager or product owner in the B2B, SaaS, or technology space, with a solid portfolio.
Demonstrated strength in customer discovery and research — you have talked to many customers and turned what you heard into product decisions.
A clear bias toward value and outcomes — comfortable challenging requests and reframing them around the underlying problem.
Strong prioritization and roadmapping discipline, with the ability to communicate decisions and trade-offs to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Solid experience in product ownership, including backlog management, requirements gathering, and specification production.
Technical ability to interact with expert developers on topics such as software architecture, databases, APIs, and user interfaces.
Proven ability to quickly learn and understand market topics and technical concepts.
Working knowledge of modern AI architectures and integration patterns (e.g., LLMs, RAG, MCP, vector databases, agents, and AI APIs), with the ability to translate emerging capabilities into enterprise product strategy and requirements.
Comfort operating with evolving scope and ambiguity — you thrive when the problem space is still taking shape.
Fluent in English and French; communication skills to collaborate, present, and evangelize the Semarchy vision and products.
Ability to handle multiple priorities simultaneously while remaining flexible and consistently hitting deadlines.

With fewer C-sections and higher VBAC success rates, our research-backed approach is delivering better outcomes. Since launching in 2021, we’ve expanded to include Preconception and Miscarriage Care, Pregnancy Care, Postpartum Support, and Gynecology. We currently have 4 clinics in the tri-state area, with three new clinics opening in 2026! Come join our team of clinicians, innovators, operators, and technologists passionate about setting a new standard in maternity care.

Full-Time

About Oula
Oula Health is a venture-backed, midwifery-led maternity and GYN care company building the next generation of women's healthcare. We partner exclusively with major health systems — including Mount Sinai, Stamford Health, and Novant Health — to embed our collaborative OB-GYN and midwifery model directly inside their networks. We're a team of ~100 people at Series B stage, with 4 clinics today and three more opening in 2026.

At Oula, our product doesn't sit alongside our EHR — it integrates directly into it. Every product and engineering decision has downstream consequences for how our EHRs are configured, and every EHR configuration decision shapes what's possible on the product side. Someone has to hold both at once.
We're looking for a technically-minded Product Manager to own and evolve our core technology stack — including our EHR, patient portal, and care management platform. This role sits at the intersection of product, operations, and health system integration, serving as the internal and external subject matter expert on our EMR and the primary lead for health system EHR integrations.
You'll manage the day-to-day health of our tech stack, partnering closely with both internal teams and external health system stakeholders to ensure our systems run smoothly and our integrations deliver.

You can sit with a midwife and understand why a clinical template matters, then turn around and write a bug ticket that engineering can actually action, then build the SOP so the next market launch doesn't require you to be in the room. When things are ambiguous (and they often are), you'll lean in rather than wait for clarity.
What You'll Own
EHR Configuration & Clinical Systems
Own day-to-day management of our core tech stack: the EHR, patient portal, and care management platform
Own Athena and Epic configuration end to end: clinical templates, order sets, lab configurations, payer connectivity, and access management for clinical and ops staff
Lead EHR integration efforts as the internal and external subject matter expert — FHIR/HL7 data exchange, health system IT coordination and committed go-live timelines
Own and accelerate Epic integration timelines as we onboard additional health system partners
Maintain configuration integrity as new markets launch and care model workflows evolve
Partner with our IT team on infrastructure; own the clinical systems layer they don't touch
Product Operations & Launch
Own bug intake and prioritization from Market Operations — standardize how Engineering receives, scopes, and resolves issues and communicates status back to the field
Build structured launch toolkits and training materials so clinic teams are prepared for new feature rollouts on day one
Coordinate end-to-end launches across Product, Engineering, and Operations
Identify where AI and automation can reduce manual administrative burden in product operations workflows
Standards & Knowledge Management
Build and maintain the clinical systems SOP library so new market setup is repeatable — documented well enough that a new hire can execute without you in the room
Develop onboarding materials for clinic managers and clinical staff on EHR workflows and tooling
Drive feature parity efforts so patients and clinicians experience a consistent standard of care across markets
Data & Reporting
Build and maintain dashboards tracking feature adoption, issue resolution, and rollout health across clinics
Develop quarterly reporting for Product, leadership, and health system partners on platform performance
Ensure data infrastructure is in place to measure the impact of every feature rollout

3+ years with product operations, technical program management, or PM-adjacent work — ideally at a growth-stage digital health or services company
Strong problem-solving instincts and genuine curiosity — you like figuring out how things work and making them work better
Ease with ambiguity and a bias toward action; this role requires you to create the playbook, not execute someone else's
Demonstrated ability to navigate complex stakeholder environments and drive aggressive timelines — ideally with client-facing or health system-facing experience
Ability to speak ‘multiple languages’ – comfort going deep on technical details while communicating clearly to non-technical audiences; you can write a bug ticket, an SOP, and a launch plan that people actually follow; hands-on EHR configuration and integration experience strongly preferred
Analytical enough to build a dashboard and identify a pattern, even if you're not a SQL expert
What Success Looks Like
In your first 90 days, you've audited our current Athena configuration, identified gaps, and have a remediation plan. You understand the bug triage process well enough to have improved it. You've met your counterparts at every health system partner and know what's coming for the next Epic integration.
At six months, new market launches have a repeatable systems and product checklist. Clinic teams know what to expect before a feature goes live. Bug resolution time is measurably faster and the field is no longer sending issues into a black hole.
At one year, the SOP library is comprehensive, clinical systems configuration is stable and documented, and you've successfully navigated at least one new health system EHR environment. The product team has a reliable partner and the ops team isn't dependent on any single person for systems knowledge.

These are the largest, most complex enterprises in the market. The ones that require deep customization, real judgment, and a partner who can operate at the highest level. This is not a standardized implementation role, and it is not an account management or customer success role.

This role owns the successful delivery, adoption, and expansion of AI solutions for Decagon's customers, serving as the primary technical and strategic owner. You earn trust with the customer's leadership team, scope a solution that solves their problems, and then build the working AI agent.

It is a rare combination: the executive influence of a top strategy consulting leader, the instincts of a product builder, and the ownership of a founder. If you have ever wanted to build the solution instead of hand off the recommendation, this role was designed for you. You own the outcome end to end, on the highest-stakes accounts in the market, with all of Decagon's cross-functional teams behind you.
This is a senior individual contributor role. You are trusted to make high-stakes decisions independently and own outcomes, gaining leverage by directing forward deployed engineers and partner teams who own a share of the execution.

Own the technical win on Decagon's largest strategic opportunities, partnering with Sales, Solutions Engineers and Forward-deployed engineers to build working AI agents that turn sophisticated, skeptical buyers into signed customers.

Design, build, and optimize enterprise-grade AI agents in production, going deep on each customer's workflows, pain points, and goals.
Turn the frameworks and playbooks you develop into reusable assets that scale across accounts and feed directly into Decagon's product roadmap.
Direct Forward-deployed engineers and partner teams to deliver at scale while you stay accountable for the outcome.
Run tight feedback loops into Product and Engineering, shaping the product based on what you learn on the front lines of our most demanding deployments.

A builder's instinct. You want to design and build the actual solution, not just diagnose the problem or manage someone else who builds it.

Experience selling, deploying, or advising on enterprise software or transformation programs at the Fortune 500 level.

The ideal candidate enjoys solving complex, high-stakes data and process problems, is naturally curious, and is always looking for ways to standardize and simplify while remaining inclusive of cultural or international differences.

· Be the Platform Expert: Act as the primary subject matter expert and trusted advisor for our Impartner PRM platform, defining and getting alignment on partner portal workflows, deal registration policies, and lead distribution procedures.

· Bridge Business & Tech: Serve as the strategic liaison between the Partner teams and technical teams, ensuring all business requirements are fully documented, articulate the “what” and “why,” and are clearly understood by platform developers.

· Map & Optimize Processes: Analyze and document "as-is" and "to-be" process flows to identify gaps, friction points for partners, and automation opportunities that can be converted into technical requirements.

· Maintain Ecosystem Compatibility: Maintain a holistic view of Salesforce and Impartner sync logic, user personas, and data flows to ensure portal configurations do not break upstream or downstream GTM systems.

· Collaborate on Architecture: Partner closely with solution architects and development teams to design clean, scalable integrations between Salesforce.com, Impartner, and adjacent marketing automation or ERP technologies.

· Drive End-to-End Delivery: Collaborate with end-users, technical squads, and change enablement teams from initial discovery through requirements gathering, build, user acceptance testing (UAT), and deployment.

· Own the PRM Roadmap: Maintain a quarterly operational roadmap of enhancements for the partner experience, targeting increased channel efficiency, accurate pipeline reporting, and readiness for scale.

· Measure What Matters: Set and track critical metrics for all initiatives. You know that a project doesn't end when a feature drops into production, but rather when partner adoption spikes and measurable operational targets are hit.

We are looking for a highly organized Project Owner to own execution quality across one of our D2C subscription products. You will be fully responsible for keeping every workstream moving to standard - setting priorities with stakeholders, translating them into clear technical tasks, driving delivery across product, engineering, design, data, and marketing, and taking direct ownership of projects that have no dedicated owner.
This is a high-accountability role suited for someone who treats "almost done" as not done. We hold a high bar: clear tickets, honest timelines, and work shipped to standard. You will inspect the work, keep the team moving when pace or quality slips, and close gaps yourself when a project falls between roles.

Execution Ownership & Process
Set priorities together with stakeholders and maintain a single, agreed backlog
Own the delivery pipeline end to end, from prioritized backlog to verified release
Define and enforce processes, definitions of done, and quality standards across all workstreams
Drive sprint planning, task tracking, and follow-through so nothing stalls silently
Identify process bottlenecks and fix them with structure, not workarounds
Task Definition & Technical Clarity
Translate product and business priorities into precise, developer-ready technical tasks
Write specs with clear acceptance criteria, edge cases, and measurable outcomes
Partner with engineering to scope, estimate, and sequence work realistically
Use AI tools daily to accelerate spec writing, analysis, and QA - and spread what works across the team
Verify delivered work against spec before it ships — and reject what falls short
Standards & Team Accountability
Hold every contributor to explicit quality and deadline expectations
Push pace and raise the bar when execution drifts, directly and constructively
Run reviews and retros that convert misses into changed processes
Institutionalize best practices so quality does not depend on individual heroics
Cross-functional & Unowned Projects
Take direct ownership of initiatives that lack a dedicated owner and drive them to completion
Coordinate across product, engineering, design, data, and marketing to unblock dependencies
Collaborate with the Managing Director to align execution priorities with business goals
Keep stakeholders informed with concise, honest status reporting

Must-Have Experience
3+ years as a Project Owner, Product Manager, or Delivery/Project Lead on a live software product
Proven track record writing technical tasks and specs that engineers execute without back-and-forth
Experience running agile delivery processes (backlog management, sprints, releases) end to end
Demonstrated ability to build processes, checklists, and quality standards - not just follow them
Experience holding cross-functional contributors accountable for deadlines and quality
Working technical fluency: able to discuss implementation trade-offs with engineers credibly
Advanced, daily use of AI tools (LLMs, agents, AI-assisted workflows) to accelerate specs, analysis, and delivery - with command of standard task-management tooling (Jira, Linear, Notion, or equivalent)
Leadership Attributes
Highly structured operator - you build systems that make quality repeatable
Comfortable giving direct, specific feedback and enforcing standards without drama
Bias to ownership: picks up unclaimed problems instead of waiting for assignment
Detail-obsessed about the work itself - reads the ticket, tests the feature, checks the numbers
Clear, direct communicator who operates effectively in a remote environment
Location
Ruby Labs operates within the CET (Central European Time) zone. Applicants from any country are welcome to apply for the position as long as they are located within approximately ± 4 hours of CET. This ensures optimal collaboration and communication during working hours.

· Experience in bringing an innovation mindset into an organisation at scale and creating sustained innovation investment across strategic horizons.

Other things to know

Learning & Development

There is no one-size-fits-all career path at Thoughtworks: however you want to develop your career is entirely up to you. But we also balance autonomy with the strength of our cultivation culture. This means your career is supported by interactive tools, numerous development programs and teammates who want to help you grow. We see value in helping each other be our best and that extends to empowering our employees in their career journeys.

We offer amazing benefits from the day you start including private medical insurance, travel insurance, income protection, critical illness, life assurance, pension scheme, personal development budget, 25 days holiday and a ride2work scheme.

We proudly, passionately and actively strive to make both Thoughtworks and our industry more representative of the communities we serve. We promote diversity in all its forms and reject discrimination and inequality. Our diversity and award winning culture inspires our thought leaders and serves to nurture and develop amazing ideas. We believe this makes us a world leading destination of choice for all technologists.

Responsible Use of AI in Recruitment

At Thoughtworks, we use AI tools to support our recruitment team with administrative tasks such as drafting communications, scheduling interviews and writing job descriptions.

Crucially, our AI tools do not screen, assess, rank or make hiring decisions. Every application is reviewed by our team and all selection decisions are made exclusively by our interviewers and hiring managers.

We are committed to fairness and responsible AI. We actively manage our AI systems by testing, monitoring for biased outcomes and implementing mitigation measures. We hold our third-party vendors to these same high standards through a rigorous governance process. For additional information, please see our full Thoughtworks AI Policy for Recruitment .

Numan is transforming health: we’ve built a cutting-edge platform that integrates diagnostics, medication, supplements, digital programmes, and doctor consultations. Giving people the tools they need to maximise life.

· Patients first.

· Learn fast.

· Own the quality.

· Succeed together.

· Care deeply.
Backed by top-tier investors, Numan is already having a positive impact on hundreds of thousands of patients here in the UK, and we want you to help us deliver this mission!

This role is about taking our platform to the next level: moving toward sophisticated, predictive, and learning-based decisioning, with a clear path toward becoming a regulated medical device.
This is a senior, high-impact individual contributor (IC) role for someone who combines deep system understanding with clinical product judgement and real experience deploying AI/ML. You move comfortably between high-level strategy and engineering-grade specifics.

Lead the product direction and roadmap for the decision platform, from long-term strategy down to the detail of how a rule actually works.
Decide which features and capabilities create the most scalable value, balancing near-term execution with strategic bets.
Establish and systematically track the success metrics for the platform.
Set the direction for how the platform uses AI and machine learning, embedding predictive and supervised learning systems into production.
Build self-learning systems so the platform continuously improves on its historical recommendations while keeping safety and explainability central.
Read and reason about system architecture. Act as a credible equal in technical debates with engineers, making sharp trade-offs between speed-to-value and long-term scalability.
Help shape the product side of the platform's regulatory direction, including the decision to build it as Software/AI as a Medical Device (SaMD).
Work fluently with sensitive patient data, partnering with clinical and quality colleagues to ensure safety and patient trust fundamentally shape the roadmap.
Proactively show engineering, clinical, design, and other product teams what the platform makes possible, while staying pragmatic about what they can absorb today.

A proven track record as a Senior or Principal Technical PM on complex platform, infrastructure, or systems products.
Hands-on experience deploying machine learning in production, specifically supervised learning or predictive systems.
Experience deploying or regulating software/AI as a medical device (SaMD), or working within closely comparable regulated frameworks.
Direct experience working with rules engines, knowledge graphs, or AI-driven decisioning systems.
Experience in clinical, healthcare, or adjacent domains handling sensitive, highly detailed user data.
Experience operating as a high-velocity individual contributor who leverages AI tools to cover ground that would traditionally require multiple people.

Dataiku is the Platform for AI Success, the enterprise orchestration layer for building, deploying, and governing AI. In a single environment, teams design and operate analytics, machine learning, and AI agents with the transparency, collaboration, and control enterprises require. Sitting above data platforms, cloud infrastructure, and AI services, Dataiku connects the full enterprise AI stack - empowering organizations to run AI across multi-vendor environments with centralized governance.

The world’s leading companies rely on Dataiku to operationalize AI and run it as a true business performance engine delivering measurable value. For more, visit the Dataiku blog , LinkedIn , X , and YouTube .

How you'll make an impact

You will play a pivotal role in shaping Dataiku's product positioning, roadmap, and requirements for predictive analytics, machine learning, and GenAI under the responsibilities of the Director of Product Management in charge of Dataiku AI/ML offering. You will work with stakeholders across all parts of the business, including Engineering, Product, GTM, Partners, Marketing Operations, and Customer Success teams, to execute growth projects and new products and features.

Your challenge is to identify and shape net new capabilities: innovations that are core additions to the product, discovered through deep customer engagement and validated before engineering commits. You are not here to maintain what exists in the long run, you will work with Technical Product Managers. You are here to find what's missing and make the case for building it.

If you're ready to step into a role where your expertise leads to tangible, wide-scale impact, where every insight you gather shapes the future of our products, we're waiting for you!

What you’ll be doing

· Embed with strategic customers to run structured discovery (interviews, async collaboration, or on-site visits) to surface unmet needs before they're obvious to competitors.

· Analyze usage and customer data to identify gaps and opportunities to enhance customer success and to deliver new capabilities with distinct business value propositions, ultimately contributing to the company's financial goals.

· Analyze market forces and competition, engage with industry analysts and Dataiku teams to execute on Dataiku’s product strategy. Collaborate with the Product Marketing team to align and deliver on product positioning messages.

· Build working prototypes (UI mockups, agentic pipeline demos, opportunity memos) to validate hypotheses with customers before engineering commits.

· Synthesize field signals across accounts to distinguish incremental customer requests from genuine innovation opportunities (net new capabilities that would be core additions to the platform.)

· Define and champion innovation initiatives from discovery through to launch, at which point ownership transitions to Technical Product Managers for ongoing improvements and maintenance.

· At launch, partner with Technical Product Managers to produce enablement material for internal customers (Product Marketing and GTM Enablement) ensuring new capabilities and big delighters land with the right positioning, messaging, and field readiness.

· Maintain the product backlog for the initiatives you own, constantly anticipating and aligning with the global product strategy and the software engineering delivery capacity.

· Participate in the development, maintenance and education on the AI/ML roadmap. Articulate your team’s technology vision, requirements, goals and milestones to stakeholders.

What you will NOT be doing

· Managing the full lifecycle of every feature you touch, your focus ends when a capability reaches steady state. You will focus on product discovery and prioritization to maximize value creation and minimize the risk of shipping the right solution to the wrong problem, not on managing maintenance priorities or driving small incremental improvements to existing capabilities.

· Product management focused on feature development, you work closely with your Technical Product Managers (PO) counterparts to ensure the engineering team gets what they need to deliver the capability at the right time, you do not dive into technical analysis.

· Shipping production solutions to customers. You build prototypes and demos to get clarity about the problem customers face or to support compelling roadmap presentations.

· Being evaluated on ARR. Example of success metrics are # of validated opportunities that made it into engineering commit, NPS of sessions with customers, time from discovery to roadmap entry.

What you’ll need to be successful

· 5+ years of experience in a similar role and a demonstrated ability to learn and thrive in front of a diverse audience in a very technical environment

· 3+ years hands-on experience with building AI/ML solutions (e.g. advanced analytics, predictive analytics, GenAI-powered applications)

· Can prototype: Build and demo agentic applications in Dataiku or elsewhere, not just slides. You don't need to be a software engineer, but you produce tangible artifacts that make ideas testable.

· Ability to engage with business leaders and influence decisions

· Proven ability to influence cross-functional teams without formal authority

What are you waiting for!

At Dataiku, you'll be part of a journey to shape the ever-evolving world of AI. We're not just building a product; we're crafting the future of AI. If you're ready to make a significant impact in a company that values innovation, collaboration, and your personal growth, we can't wait to welcome you to Dataiku! Docker has been one of the most loved brands in developer tooling, trusted by more than 20 million monthly users and over 20 billion container image pulls. From solo founders to the world's largest companies, developers rely on Docker to build, share, and run their applications across our suite of products including Docker Desktop, Docker Hub, and Docker Scout.
We are a globally distributed, remote-first team building the tools that define how software gets built and delivered. As AI agents redefine software development, Docker is at the center of that shift, providing the sandboxed environments, verified images, and secure infrastructure that make autonomous workflows trustworthy by default.

The Products Team at Docker is looking for a Principal Product Manager for our core Sandbox platform. You will own and drive an investment and product area from high-level concept design to delivery and operation. You will help shape the future of a key area of Docker.

You will work closely with developers inside and outside of Docker, our customers, as well as our partners to expand our open ecosystem offering and provide value. As the company and ecosystem grows, you will help to foster teams eager to continuously build, measure, and learn.
To thrive in this role, you’ll need experience working with developers and a technical knowledge of developer tools. You’ll need to know how to work with the developer community and understand the lifecycle of software development, the software supply chain and how AI agents are safely orchestrated and deployed with sandboxes.

You’ll need a relentless drive to try new things, and an eye for detail. Your long-term success will depend on your ability to own the product roadmap and collaborate with the developer community, and scale our services.

Most importantly, you’ll need to be okay with taking ownership of big objectives with big goals, working with a cross-functional team, and maintaining a bias for action.

You own a product area, the long-term vision, the roadmap, the revenue, and the results.
You believe in and can articulate succinctly, our customers and their pain points. You empathize and understand the world they live in and the constraints they work through.
You will engage deeply with developers and find amazing solutions that solve today's problems while optimizing for tomorrow's vision.
You enjoy building products that are easy to adopt and use. You have a keen design sensibility, and you are always looking for ways to improve the usability of your products.
You are comfortable with ambiguity and will guide product definition, feature prioritization, and scope, in concert with cross functional teams.
You’re a fan of iterative development, working with our customers as well as cross-functional teams to hypothesize, measure impact, and learn from previous releases to iterate on future roadmap plans.

You have deep empathy for the needs of developers and are obsessed with talking to your users.
You have created and deployed AI agents at scale and dealt with all the challenges and pain points of such tasks
You are comfortable interacting with a command-line interface.
You have experience building B2B, SaaS or have a background in Public Cloud
You have experience working with tools in the software supply chain and/or software security
You can break down complex technical problems into small, release-able, user valuable features.

You can analyze data, both qualitative and quantitative, to inform decision making.

You are a doer as well as a strategist. We are small and need all hands on deck.

Airtm is a financial-infrastructure company building the future of the online-work economy. We are on a mission to empower the world's growing number of Digital Entrepreneurs in the Global South, giving them the financial freedom to thrive.
The problem is clear: in emerging markets, accessing the dollar economy is difficult. Cross-border payments are slow, expensive, and often lose value to inflation. This limits the potential of millions of talented individuals.
Airtm’s solution is a swift and comprehensive financial platform that facilitates low-value cross-border payments and local cash-outs. As pioneers in stablecoin-payment infrastructure, Airtm has built the most advanced cross-border payment system available on the market.
As a company married to the world of online work, Airtm will go beyond payments to build the necessary infrastructure the online-work economy needs to thrive. We are fostering an entirely new economy, giving individuals, communities, and countries the tools to take control of their financial destinies.

This is a high-impact role for someone who can connect vision with execution. You'll shape the roadmap, align cross-functional teams, and build scalable solutions involving blockchain products, leveraging AI to solve critical needs for our users and move faster than the competition.

Translate vision into a realistic, high-leverage roadmap and backlog that balances short-term growth with long-term scalability.
Collaborate with engineering, design, legal, compliance, and commercial teams to build and ship features that drive user adoption.
Work closely with growth and marketing to accelerate go-to-market adoption and unlock new revenue streams.
Identify and champion opportunities to embed AI powered capabilities directly into the product, from intelligent automation and personalization to surfacing insights that help users make better financial decisions.
Use AI tools actively in your day-to-day workflow for research, spec writing, competitive analysis, data synthesis and help raise the bar for how the broader team works.

In just five years, Stora has become the platform behind more than 30% of UK self storage locations, and we're scaling globally from here. Operators have processed over £150m in automated payments through us, and see an average of 32% business growth after they switch.
We're doing this in a market that's wide open. Europe has over 10,000 self storage sites and is growing fast, yet it sits years behind the US on maturity and is still barely touched by good software. The UK is our stronghold. The rest of Europe is where we're heading next.
Stora is the operating system for modern self storage: online bookings, payments, facility management, reporting, and automation in one platform. We started as operators ourselves, and that's still how we think. If you want to own a product operators depend on every day, in a company genuinely rethinking how it builds, this is it.
Why this role matters
We have a strong product team, great engineers, and a growing product. The bottleneck isn't ideas or execution capacity. It's people who can hold the full picture at once.
What the business needs, what the customer actually experiences, what's technically feasible, what to cut when time is short, and knowing when to slow down. Making good calls across all of it. That's the job.
We've shortened the loop between insight and shipped product by stripping out the layers that slow good judgement down. The quality bar didn't move. This role exists to keep doing that. It carries real ownership from day one, and the scope grows as Stora does.
The surface you'd own
This is the product operators live in every day, and the storefront their own customers book through. You're designing for two users at once: the operator running the business, and the end customer renting the unit. Getting that B2B2C experience right is a genuine craft problem. It's a broad, central surface, and it's heavy on UX.

Core workflows: customers, units, tenancies, access
Roles, permissions, account structure
Operational reporting: occupancy, utilisation, activity
The internal data layer: event tracking, core models, metric definitions
The growth surface: storefront, checkout, the lead → booking funnel
If an operator uses it daily, or relies on it to understand their business, it sits with this team.
How we actually work
We've changed how product gets built at Stora. This is how we operate now.
Designers work directly in the codebase. Engineers and product people work closely together from the start. We use AI genuinely: to explore, prototype and move faster. The work gets closer to reality, sooner.
If you're at a company that talks about moving faster but runs the same process it did three years ago, this will feel different. We're not done evolving how we work, and this person will have real scope to shape that.

Own a problem space end-to-end, from understanding the customer need to something live in the product
Work across both sides of the experience: operator back office and end-customer storefront
Work directly with engineering leads. Close collaboration, not handoff
Make scope calls. Know what to cut, what's fundamental, what can wait
Work with or without a designer, depending on the problem. What matters is the outcome
Stay close to customers, talk to operators, understand how they run their businesses, bring that into every decision
Shape how we work. The process isn't fixed. If something's slowing things down, fix it

Real product experience at a SaaS company. You've owned features or problem spaces end-to-end and shipped things people use. Roughly 2+ years, though we care more about the evidence than the number
A builder by instinct. You make things: side projects, tools, a company you tried to start. We'd rather see someone who ships than someone who only plans
A design or engineering past works too. You may have come from design, engineering, or somewhere else entirely. Designers and people who've started their own things tend to do well here
Great product taste. You can tell the difference between a solution that works and one that just ships
You define it yourself. You don't need everything defined to make progress
Real design sense. Strong enough to contribute or push back, which matters a lot on a surface this UX-heavy
AI-native. You use AI as a natural part of how you think and work. Not waiting to be shown how
This role is not for you if
You need a detailed brief before you can start
You've only ever worked inside someone else's process and haven't shipped anything of your own
You think good product work stops before it ships
You go quiet when a problem is ambiguous instead of pushing into it
Why Stora
A category-defining surface to own. Self storage software is wide open, and the core experience is the heart of it. You set the direction here, you don't inherit it.
Work that ships, and that you feel. We've stripped out the layers between insight and shipped product. What you build reaches operators in weeks, not quarters.
A team that builds differently. Designers in the codebase, AI used for real, process that bends when it should. Small team, outsized impact.

Share options
Remote across the UK & Europe, or hybrid from our Belfast office
35 days holiday
Private health insurance (for you + family)
Company pension plan
Apple hardware
Learning & development support
Next steps
When you apply, we'll ask for a link to something you've made — a product, a side project, a repo, a tool you built because something annoyed you. It doesn't need to be polished, successful, or related to storage. We just want to see that you build. Please include one.
We're reviewing applications as they come in and will be in touch quickly if it looks like a match.

Bnberry is transforming the $87 billion travel tech industry by changing how hotels and resorts connect with guests worldwide. We’re building DBS — a new kind of product that hotels adopt as a B2B SaaS business tool, and that travelers experience directly as a consumer-facing hotel booking journey.
This is not a Product Owner or delivery-management role focused on writing tickets and managing developers. Your mandate is to own DBS end-to-end, connecting three product areas that most companies keep separate: the guest-facing booking experience, the hotel-facing workflows and business value, and how travelers discover hotels through search and AI tools.
What You’ll Own
The consumer-facing booking journey — including the logic behind it: availability, rates, cancellation policies, and how PMS/CRS or booking-engine integrations shape what the guest sees
Hotel-facing workflows tied to DBS: onboarding, reporting, and adoption
The product capabilities that help hotels improve and measure visibility across search engines and AI discovery tools, in partnership with Marketing and relevant specialists
Booking-funnel performance and conversion
The link between guest experience and measurable hotel business value

Define product vision and roadmap for DBS, connecting guest booking UX, hotel workflows, and AI discovery into one coherent product
Own the booking journey end-to-end — identify friction in calendars, date selection, room/rate selection, checkout, and confirmation, and understand how availability, rates, cancellation policies, and PMS/CRS or booking-engine integrations affect what the guest experiences; work with Engineering on dependencies and failure cases
Translate hotel onboarding, reporting, and adoption needs into product decisions that show measurable business value to hotel customers
Own the product capabilities behind search and AI/GEO visibility — partner with Marketing and relevant specialists on execution, while building enough SEO/GEO literacy to identify and prioritize the right product bets
Interview hoteliers and travelers and run usability tests; translate qualitative and quantitative findings into clear priorities
Define success metrics before building, and use experiment results to guide iteration
Work closely with Design and Engineering through detailed user journeys, making trade-offs and shipping in small, practical iterations
Align Engineering, Design, Sales, and Customer Success around DBS priorities, and take responsibility for product outcomes

3+ years of product management experience owning customer-facing products, including relevant experience in hospitality technology or travel booking
Relevant, demonstrable connection to the US market
Hands-on customer research skills — hotelier and traveler interviews, usability testing, and translating findings into clear priorities
Strong analytical and experimentation skills — diagnosing booking-funnel friction, testing improvements, and measuring booking conversion, hotel adoption, and retention
Comfortable working through detailed user journeys with Design and Engineering, making trade-offs, and shipping in small iterations
Able to operate independently with ambiguity, prioritize by customer and business value, and align Engineering, Design, Sales, and Customer Success

Industry-Grounded — You’ve worked in hotel technology, B2B hospitality platforms, or a B2C travel product with an actual booking journey. Deep exposure to hotel distribution systems is a plus, not a prerequisite — strong B2C travel/booking experience counts too.
US Market Fluent — You have demonstrable familiarity with US hotels or travel customers, whether through working with them directly or through living and studying in the US combined with hospitality experience.
Booking UX Owner — You understand the details of a booking flow — calendars, date selection, room and rate choice, checkout, confirmation — and the logic behind it: availability, rates, cancellation policies, and PMS/CRS or booking-engine integrations. You can spot friction before a customer complains about it.
Fluent in Both Guest and Hotel — You’re as comfortable reasoning about a traveler’s booking journey as you are about a hotelier’s onboarding, adoption, and ROI.
Fast Learner on AI/SEO — You understand how travelers discover hotels through search and AI tools, and can pick up emerging SEO/GEO capabilities quickly enough to know which product bets are worth making — without needing to personally execute SEO.
Success Metrics
Examples include: booking conversion rate, hotel adoption of DBS, feature adoption, booking-funnel completion, search and AI/GEO visibility for hotels on DBS, customer and hotelier satisfaction, and retention.
Important Clarification
This role is not a traditional Product Owner responsible primarily for backlog management and task assignment. The focus is on owning DBS as a genuinely new product category — one that has to work as a business tool for hotels and as a booking experience travelers actually use.

Define a new product category — DBS sits at the intersection of B2B SaaS, consumer booking, and AI discovery, largely undefined by competitors today
Autonomy to experiment, take risks, and drive discovery
Work at the intersection of cutting-edge AI and a massive traditional industry

The opportunity
We're looking for a Staff Product Manager to lead the strategy for Trucking Technology—the systems that plan, procure, dispatch, and settle every truck move in North America—and drive the unification of our fragmented ground transportation business into a single Flexport-owned platform by 2027. You will define the vision for how planning, procurement, and carrier experience integrate into one operating system and execute with high autonomy.

By owning the full stack, we will consolidate demand, capture leaking margin, and deliver a high-quality experience across modes. You will also drive the next generation of trucking automation—including AI-driven appointment scheduling and automated dispatch—to continue the strategic initiatives in our annual operating plan.
Sitting at the intersection of product, operations, and business, you will be measured by operational and financial impact rather than just features shipped. This role involves redesigning the operating processes themselves and persuading leadership to adopt new models. You will also raise the bar for the PM team through mentorship and sharper frameworks on our most complex product problems.
You will raise the bar for the PM team through mentorship, better frameworks, and sharper thinking on the hardest product problems we face. Own the vision and strategy for Flexport's unified Trucking Technology stack across planning, procurement, pricing, and carrier experience.

Reengineer and digitize underlying trucking workflows to establish a leaner operating model.
Modernize the carrier experience to reduce friction across load acceptance, scheduling, and payment touchpoints.
Collaborate with global Engineering, Design, and Operations teams to translate complex logistics workflows into intuitive systems.
Use data-driven frameworks to guide investment and represent your domain in strategic leadership forums.
Mentor PMs to raise the bar for product specs, prioritization, and communication across the team.

Revenue Growth Management (RGM) is one of The Coca-Cola Company's most important commercial capabilities, and not simply a pricing discipline. Coca-Cola positions RGM alongside brand building, innovation, and integrated execution as a core capability for topline growth, and our growth strategy names it a key commercial capability for determining where to play and how to win.
RGM connects consumer demand to the economics of the system. It determines what we sell, in which packages, at what price points, through which channels and customers, and with what promotional investment, all in service of balanced growth across transactions, volume, and price/mix.

Done well, it finds incremental revenue pools and converts them into commercial action, improves the economics of every price, pack, assortment, and promotion decision, builds the affordability and premiumization ladders that bring more consumers into the portfolio, and gives Coca-Cola and its bottlers a common fact base for growing customer revenue and profit rather than simply negotiating price.
We are now reimagining RGM for the agentic AI era, and we are building it ourselves.

Our Global RGM Product is evolving from a suite of analytical solutions into an intelligent decision platform where AI agents interact directly with enterprise data, invoke advanced analytics and optimization models, run and compare scenarios, and hand commercial teams a recommendation with the reasoning attached.

Work that once took an analyst a week (pulling the data, running the model, writing the story, defending the number) is being compressed into a conversation.
Few companies are attempting this at this scale, and fewer are still against decisions this consequential: real pricing, promotion, and portfolio moves, made across markets and bottlers. The work sits at the frontier of the CPG industry, spanning agent orchestration, retrieval over enterprise data, and the evaluation of non-deterministic and deterministic systems, and none of it is a research exercise. What we build ships to commercial teams who use it to make decisions the same week.
This is an opportunity to build, not just design, the next generation of commercial decision intelligence at Coca-Cola, and to establish the operating model for agentic RGM at global scale. The patterns set here will shape how one of the world's largest commercial systems makes its most important decisions. If you want your work in front of real users, at real scale, from the first release, this is that role.

As Product Manager, RGM, you will own the what and the why of the Global RGM product: which problems it solves, for whom, in what order, and how success is measured. You will work within a persistent, cross-functional product team alongside Data Science, Engineering, UX, Architecture, and RGM experts. Engineering owns how the product is built; you own everything that determines whether it is worth building.
Product direction starts in market. You will spend time with RGM teams at operating units and bottlers to understand how pricing, promotion, and portfolio decisions are actually made, where current ways of working break down, and which problems are worth solving next. You will convert that discovery into direction: clear problem statements, a prioritized roadmap, and requirements that tell the team not just what to build, but why it matters commercially.
Day to day, this is a product ownership seat. You will write user stories and acceptance criteria, prioritize the backlog against commercial value, define what 'good' looks like for each release, and sign off that what shipped does what the business needed.

It demands genuine fluency in what the product produces (elasticities, uplift against baseline, share math) and in the commercial world those recommendations land in.

You will stay engaged across the full product lifecycle, from discovery and pilot design through launch, adoption measurement, and continuous improvement - because adoption is the truest test of whether you defined the right product.
The role is global across a commercial system that spans more than 200 countries and territories, roughly 200 bottling partners, and 30 million retail customer outlets - few products anywhere offer a larger canvas. It is also a first seat: the product discipline you establish here becomes the pattern for how the Global RGM Product scales to every market.

s.h: What You Will Do for Us
s.t:
Own the product roadmap for the Global RGM suite: define the problems worth solving, sequence capabilities by commercial value, and present the roadmap and the value delivered to OU leadership and bottler executives.
Run continuous discovery with users: sit with RGM managers and walk a run end to end (which price moves to take, which to skip, and why) to understand where the product creates value and where it falls short.
Translate discovery into direction: turn user pain into written requirements with clear problem statements, examples, and acceptance criteria, and retest with the same users once a fix ships.
Write user stories the engineering team can build against, and represent the voice of OUs and bottlers in prioritization and roadmap decisions with the Global RGM Product Owner.
Own and prioritize the product backlog against commercial value, with the judgment to say no, sequence competing requests, and defend a prioritization call to senior stakeholders.
Define the success measures for each release, participate in backlog refinement and sprint reviews with the pod, and give business sign-off that shipped functionality does what the market actually needed.
Guard the product's credibility by catching recommendations that would not survive scrutiny in front of a bottler, before the bottler sees them.
Embed the closed-loop RGM workflow in the product (insight generation and opportunity sizing, strategy setting, guardrail definition, in-market execution, and post-implementation evaluation) so markets operate a consistent, repeatable process.
Design for governance: make RGM rules of engagement (price floors and ceilings, discount depth and promotion frequency, and price-gap and price-index thresholds) capabilities the product enforces rather than policies applied around it.
Support pilot design and test-and-learn discipline with market teams: hypothesis framing, control groups, and incrementality measurement.
Partner with the AI engineer on insight quality, rating generated insights and flagging output the underlying data does not support.
Partner with the UX designer on launch communication, naming, and demo material so each release lands with the business.
Build the business case for significant capability requests: size the commercial opportunity, weigh it against effort and alternatives, and make the call on what is worth building.
Lead each release to adoption: launch planning, capability building, and short playbooks (how to read an elasticity, when to trust a recommendation), with the goal of users opening the product without you.

As our Global Product Manager for Sustaining Hardware within Philips Ambulatory & Monitoring Diagnostics (AM&D), you will be accountable for the ongoing lifecycle management of the MCT and Holter devices.

These mature products remain critical to customers and operations as development progresses on the next-generation sensor and you will translate quality, regulatory, customer, service, supply, and operational needs into clear product priorities and coordinated execution that protects product performance, availability, compliance, and continuity.

Partner with Quality and Regulatory on complaint trends, CAPA, risk management, post-market surveillance, audits, and regulatory documentation, ensuring product management inputs and decisions are complete, timely, and traceable.
Monitor product health using relevant performance indicators, including complaints, returns, reliability, service burden, supply availability, cost, and customer feedback; identify trends and drive corrective or improvement actions. Support supply continuity, lifecycle transition, and end-of-life planning, including demand and inventory considerations, component availability, regional impacts, customer transition needs, and alignment with next-generation sensor plans.
Provide product expertise to Sales, Marketing, Service, Operations, and regional teams; maintain current product documentation, roadmap and status, and stakeholder alignment, and escalate risks and trade-offs with clear recommendations.

## **Das sollten Sie über uns wissen** ##
Everllence ebnet den Weg in eine klimaneutrale Weltwirtschaft. Ob Industrieproduktion, Energie- oder maritime Wirtschaft: Wir denken ganzheitlich und packen schon heute die Herausforderungen von morgen an - für eine nachhaltige Wertschöpfung unserer Kunden. In unserem Technologieportfolio steckt die Erfahrung aus über 250 Jahren Ingenieurstradition.

Everllence hat seinen Hauptsitz in Deutschland und beschäftigt rund 15.000 Mitarbeiter an mehr als 120 Standorten weltweit. Unsere Kunden profitieren außerdem vom globalen Service-Center-Netzwerk unserer After-Sales Marke, Everllence PrimeServ.
## **Folgende Aufgaben können wir Ihnen anbieten** ##
* **Produktstrategie:** Entwicklung und Umsetzung von Produktstrategien zur Unterstützung des Vertriebsteams. Der Produktmanager ist ein Mitglied des Verkaufsteams, spielt eine sehr wichtige Rolle innerhalb des Teams und ist für die Erreichung der Verkaufsziele verantwortlich.
* **Marktanalyse:** Führen Sie Markt- und Wettbewerbsanalysen durch, um Trends, Marktentwicklungen, Potenziale, Kundenbedürfnisse und Möglichkeiten für Produktinnovationen zu ermitteln.
* **Funktionsübergreifende Zusammenarbeit: **Arbeiten Sie eng mit den Teams für Forschung und Entwicklung, Technik, Vertrieb, Marketing und Kundenbetreuung zusammen, um eine erfolgreiche Produktentwicklung und -Einführung sicherzustellen.
* **Projektleitung:** Überwachen Sie Produktentwicklungsprojekte vom Konzept bis zur Markteinführung und stellen Sie sicher, dass Zeitpläne und Budgets eingehalten werden, und verwalten Sie das gesamte Produktportfolio.
* **Einbindung der Kunden:** Einbindung der Kunden, um Feedback einzuholen, ihre Bedürfnisse zu verstehen und die Produktzufriedenheit sicherzustellen.
* **Leistungsüberwachung:** Überwachen Sie die Produktleistung und treffen Sie datengestützte Entscheidungen, um das Produktangebot zu verbessern, und erstatten Sie dem Management bei Bedarf Bericht.
* **Einhaltung gesetzlicher Vorschriften:** Sicherstellen, dass alle Produkte den einschlägigen Industrienormen und Vorschriften entsprechen.

**Are you passionate about data, AI, and turning ideas into products that create real business impact? **
Do you want to work in a dynamic, cross-functional environment where you can bridge business needs with cutting-edge AI solutions? If yes, this is your opportunity to join our Property & Casualty AI Transformation team in Zurich and help shape the future of AI adoption in the (re)insurance industry.
We are looking for an AI Product Owner who thrives at the intersection of AI, product, and business. In this role, you will combine hands-on AI engineering expertise with software product and delivery leadership, building scalable AI solutions that create measurable business impact across underwriting, claims and operations.
You-ll be part of our Property & Casualty AI Transformation team, whose mission is to harness advanced analytics and AI to create a competitive advantage for our business. We work closely with business stakeholders in underwriting, claims and operations and Data & Tech teams to design, deliver, and scale AI solutions that enhance decision-making, improve productivity, and drive better outcomes across the organization.

s.h: As an AI Product Owner, you will
s.t:
* Own the delivery of AI products, from concept to deployment and integration into user applications.
* Act as a stakeholder partner, aligning product roadmaps and delivery with business strategic objectives and technology landscapes to harness the power of AI in our underwriting, claims and operations processes.
* Build scalable data pipelines and AI applications, ensuring robustness, performance, and enterprise-grade quality.
* Lead cross-functional delivery, working closely with AI engineers, data scientists, software engineers and business experts to bring AI solutions into production.
* Help shape the standards and best practices for GenAI implementation, AI product governance, and responsible AI use across the company.
* Stay at the forefront of emerging AI technologies and methodologies, evaluating their practical business application.

* Drive and shape AI products from business problem and value hypothesis through production and scale.
* Collaborate with cross-functional teams and stakeholders to understand and translate underwriting, claims or operations business requirements into clear product requirements and actionable delivery plans.
* Design and develop user-centric AI applications in Python/PySpark, that align with business and technological requirements, emphasizing user experience & data storytelling.
* Build and manage product roadmaps, priorities and backlogs, balancing business value, user needs, technical feasibility and strategic objectives.
* Define success measures and use data, user feedback and business outcomes to continuously improve AI products.
* Manage stakeholder relationships and create alignment across business, Digital &Tech stakeholders and governance functions.
* Ensure AI solutions meet appropriate standards for quality, scalability, security and responsible AI
* Continuously evaluate emerging AI technologies and identify opportunities to apply them to real business challenges.

s.h: To be successful in the role, you bring
s.t:
* A university degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, or a related Quantitative or technical field.
* 5+ years- experience designing and delivering enterprise-grade AI/GenAI or data-driven products.
* Hands-on experience with GenAI solution implementation, understanding strength and limitations of models, and AI models from training and testing to deployment in production.
* Strong proficiency in Python/PySpark and software development best practices.
* Expertise in data pipelines and MLOps practices at scale.
* Strong product thinking and the ability to connect business problems, user needs and technology.
* Proven ability to manage senior stakeholders and lead delivery across business and tech teams.
* Excellent communication skills in English, with the ability to make complex technical topics understandable and relevant to business audiences.
If you also have the following experience and interests, it is a huge plus:
* Knowledge of Azure, Palantir Foundry and Typescript.
* Building applications using LLMs, RAG, agents or other modern GenAI patterns.
* Project management or delivery within agile environments.
* Experience working in a multinational or cross-cultural environment.

* Work on high-impact AI projects that combine strategic influence with hands-on engineering.
* Join a diverse, collaborative, and innovative team in Zurich.
* Grow your career in a global organization committed to responsible and impactful AI.

In addition to your base salary, Swiss Re offers an attractive performance-based variable compensation component, designed to recognise your achievements. Further you will enjoy a variety of global and location specific benefits.

Higharc is a VC-backed startup that is changing how new homes are designed and built. Join a founding team who’ve shipped products for Autodesk, Electronic Arts, Nike, and Apple. We have raised over $175M with support from top-notch venture capital firms and more than 18 strategic investors: industry leaders in construction, building products manufacturing, and distribution.
Higharc is seeking a hands-on Forward Deployed Product Manager to turn a large production homebuilder's unstructured plan catalog into structured, queryable product data. This is a founding role on a brand-new Forward Deployed team.

A homebuilder's plan library is the product data behind its entire business, and at enterprise scale that data is almost entirely unstructured. Plans live as drawing sets scattered across semi-autonomous divisions, renamed and re-numbered as they move. Nobody can say with confidence which plans are duplicates, how many versions of a given home exist, or what actually varies between them.
Higharc converts those catalogs into structured, queryable plan data and builds the analysis on top of it: searchable plan libraries with agent-enabled natural-language search, geometric similarity scoring that surfaces plans which have forked under different names, structured mapping of what varies across a library, and classification that makes consolidation decisions possible.
You'll own what gets built in the field, working embedded alongside our Forward Deployed Engineers and in partnership with the homebuilder to turn plans into actionable data. This is a role for someone who wants to be close to where the problem lives. Higharc is fully remote; you can sit anywhere in the continental U.S., with travel to client sites and company events up to 30% of the time.

Embed with HQ, regional, and division teams to run discovery—locate plan assets, establish source of truth, and document how each division represents its plans and where variation originates.
Own product definition for the searchable plan library, analytics dashboard, and agent-enabled search—what a good query looks like, what a useful answer looks like, and what "structured for analysis" actually means.
Tune Higharc's Autotranslate AI to identify, categorize, and translate floorplans into data.
Work hands-on with the data: query the structured plan library directly, build against our internal APIs, and ship working capability back to users rather than filing a ticket and waiting.
Define acceptance criteria for delivery milestones—coverage targets, data-field completeness, QA error thresholds—and hold the line on them when schedule pressure argues otherwise.
Frame and defend quantifiable ROI: redundancy across a catalog, dimensional spread on repeated conditions, consolidation candidates, and the purchasing leverage each one represents.
Partner with Forward Deployed Engineering, the Technical Lead, QA, Intake Specialists, and Client Strategy, and present progress and tradeoffs to executive stakeholders.
Capture the playbooks, artifacts, and data patterns that let the forward deployed model carry over to the next engagement.

You're a product manager who is happiest closest to the customer, and you've learned that the fastest path to the right answer is usually to go look. You're comfortable being handed a scope that is 70% specified and a data set nobody has structured before. You can hold a conversation with an architect about how a plan set is drawn in the morning and write the query that tests your hypothesis about it in the afternoon.
You know the difference between a demo and a deliverable, and you're honest with customers about which one they're looking at.

5+ years of product management experience, including significant time in customer-facing or deployed settings—enterprise implementations, solutions engineering, technical consulting, or professional services.
Hands-on technical fluency: you write SQL, work in notebooks, script against APIs, and interrogate a data set yourself rather than requesting a pull.
Experience prototyping to validate ideas quickly using tools like Cursor, Replit, or V0.dev .
A track record defining structured data models, taxonomies, or classification schemes and getting a business to actually adopt them.
Strong judgment about data quality—what level of accuracy a decision requires, and what it costs to get there.
Excellent written and verbal communication, including with executive stakeholders who have limited time and no patience for status without substance.
Willingness to travel to client sites and company events up to 30% of the time.

Traditional banking has never really given you control over your financial life. Satispay exists to change that: to empower people through finance . That means making financial services easy and accessible for over 6.5M users.
We started with payments, then benefits, investing, cards... and we’re not done. Not even close. We follow the same logic every time: find a real problem, solve it properly, then look for the next one. The destination? To build the most loved financial platform in the world.

If you own outcomes rather than tasks, stay close to what users need, and refuse to wait for someone else to fix what's broken — you'll find people here who work exactly in the same way. And together, you'll build something worth being proud of.
What you'll be doing
As our Product Manager - Payments, you'll take full ownership of Consumer Payments within the Features & Payment domain — spanning debit cards, SEPA Credit Transfers, QR payments, and more — building and scaling the products millions of people use every day. Here's what that looks like in practice:
Discover the Right Problems – Combine direct user evidence with product data, market signals and regulatory insight to frame and validate problems before and during delivery, not only at kick-off.
0→1 Product Leadership – Drive strategy and execution for new payment products and features, from first concept to launch.
Scaling What Works – Take live products beyond launch: grow adoption and activation, expand coverage and use cases, and harden reliability as volumes increase. Treat adoption, reliability, support demand and realised value as product outcomes, not launch metrics.
Consumer-Facing Experience – Own the UX and customer-facing side of payments, ensuring complex financial mechanics are intuitive, transparent and seamlessly integrated into Satispay.
Product Definition & Documentation – Write clear Product Requirements for Engineering and stakeholders, carrying the user's perspective into every decision.
Cross-functional Alignment – Act as a strategic orchestrator across Customer Care, Finance, Compliance, Marketing, Legal and FinCrime/Fraud to align priorities around a shared product vision — designing experiences that meet regulatory requirements such as PSD2, SCA and AML rather than working around them.
External Partnerships – Work alongside our scheme and delivery managers on relationships with card schemes, issuing processors and payment providers: shape the roadmap you depend on, hold partners to their commitments, and turn their capabilities into user value.
Data-Driven Optimisation – Analyse product usage and performance metrics to optimise payment features and uncover new market opportunities.
Process Evangelism & Mentorship – Advocate for thorough documentation and efficient workflows to help the team anticipate obstacles and ensure smooth product delivery.

This role needs someone who can hold both sides of payments: the consumer experience and the rails underneath it.
Product Experience – 3+ years as a Product Manager in payments, banking or fintech.
Launch & Scale Track Record – Proven experience shipping products from scratch and growing live products through their scaling phase.
Payments Fluency – Deep experience with at least one payment rail — card issuing, SEPA transfers or account-to-account — and enough familiarity with the mechanics behind them (authorisation and settlement, scheme flows, chargebacks and disputes) to hold a conversation with Engineering and providers alike.
Financial & Analytical Skills – Strong grasp of payment economics — interchange and scheme fees, provider costs, fraud losses — and the ability to build a business case and read performance data without waiting for BI.
Regulated-Environment Comfort – Ability to design great experiences within regulatory constraints (PSD2, SCA, AML) and to treat Compliance, Legal and Fraud as partners rather than gatekeepers.
Stakeholder Management – Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with senior stakeholders and cross-functional teams (Engineering, UX, BI, Finance, Compliance).
Language Skills – Professional fluency in English. Italian isn't required — we work in English .
Don't worry if you don't tick every box. We believe in the power of different viewpoints and strengths. Your unique perspective is important as we build something special: if you're passionate and can make a difference, we truly encourage you to apply.
