About Supabase
Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.
More than 10 million developers build on it, from solo founders shipping over a weekend to teams and builders via Vercel, Lovable and Stripe, and every one of them reaches Supabase through a surface: an API, an auth flow, an SDK, or a Partner's product with Supabase integrated.
The current and next wave of software leans on those surfaces harder than any before it.
Agents now act on behalf of developers and end users, authentication has to work machine-to-machine as seamlessly as it once worked human-to-human, and independent platforms increasingly need to authenticate, delegate, and coordinate with each other without a person in the loop.

For a platform built on Postgres with Auth, Compute, Storage and generated Data APIs at its core, the surfaces where Supabase meets Partners and their systems are some of the most important avenues that we own - this role owns these surfaces.
This role owns a focused portfolio of those Partners. Not the platform as a whole, but a small number of strategic Partners whose integrations you are accountable for making excellent. Success here is a product measure, not a commercial one: the integration is high quality, the developers who use it are well served, and it keeps improving.

That means living close to those developers, obsessing over where the integration fails them, and turning what you learn into the roadmap. It is a product and engineering job first, because the best integrations are won in architecture reviews and pull requests, not in meetings.
What You'll Be Responsible For
Owning the success of a focused portfolio of strategic Partners, a small number of them rather than the platform as a whole. You are accountable for the outcome of each partnership: a high-quality integration that the developers who use it reach for, and that keeps getting better.
Living close to the developers who use these integrations. Talking to them constantly, finding where each integration breaks down in real use, and building the roadmap from that signal rather than from a Partner's wishlist.
Deciding the right integration model for each Partner: what Supabase owns, what the Partner owns, what you build jointly, and what stays open and Partner-agnostic, reading whether the two roadmaps run together or diverge and choosing accordingly.
Working hands-on with each Partner's product and engineering counterparts to ship. Holding your own in an architecture review and a code-level design discussion, and turning strategy into shipped, high-quality integrations rather than long conversations.
Setting the quality bar for what a great integration looks like, and building the mechanisms (documentation, tooling, guardrails, versioning) that hold every Partner to it as adoption scales.
Defining what success looks like for each integration and measure it honestly: adoption by the developers who use it, integration quality, and reliability in real use. Using those signals to decide how deep to go with each Partner and where to push the integration next.

s.h: You Might Be a Good Fit If You
s.t:
Have 7+ years of product management on developer tools, or are an ex-founder with strong product instincts, and are technical enough to read an architecture doc, follow a design discussion, and ask the right questions.
Are based in the San Francisco Bay Area. While we hire globally for almost all roles, this role requires being located near SF (please note we don't sponsor work visa or relocations, you already need to be based in the Bay Area).
Have shipped integration or platform surfaces that other companies' systems build against, owning APIs, auth or identity flows, or developer-facing platform surfaces end to end, and can reason at the product level about how two independent systems should authenticate and exchange data: where to be open, where to be strict, and where trust lies in these integrations.

Familiarity with more recent primitives like workers/agent sandboxes and developer-tooling products, or with machine-to-machine authentication, is a bonus.
Are biased toward speed, and would rather ship something imperfect (but secure) while learning than spend another month polishing a spec.
Build with what you own, using the surfaces on your roadmap the way a Partner would: standing up an auth flow, calling the Data API, deploying a database, wiring Supabase into another product. You form opinions through first-hand use.
Comfortable using AI tools to compress the slower parts of the role, like research, drafting, and synthesising feedback, so you spend more time on judgment calls.
Work async by default. Supabase is fully remote, so you make decisions in writing and move work forward without meetings.

Fully Remote
We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.
Tech Allowance
Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.
Annual Off-Sites
Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.
Flexible Work
We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.
Professional Development
Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.
~400 team members
60+ countries
20+ languages spoken
Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)
540,000+ community members
We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

Synthesia is the world’s leading AI video platform for business, used by over 90% of the Fortune 100. Founded in 2017, the company is headquartered in London, with offices and teams across Europe and the US.
As AI continues to shape the way we live and work, Synthesia develops products to enhance visual communication and enterprise skill development, helping people work better and stay at the center of successful organizations.
Following our recent Series E funding round, where we raised $200 million, our valuation stands at $4 billion. Our total funding exceeds $530 million from premier investors including Accel, NVentures (Nvidia's VC arm), Kleiner Perkins, GV, and Evantic Capital, alongside the founders and operators of Stripe, Datadog, Miro, and Webflow.

Synthesia ships more product, faster, than we ever have. AI has collapsed the cost of building which means the hard part is no longer making things, it’s making sure people actually adopt them. That’s the job of Growth, and we’re changing how we do it: instead of bolting Growth on after launch to optimise, we’re embedding a Growth PM into every core bet from day one, so how a product acquires, activates and scales is designed in from the first cycle.
We’re hiring a Growth Product Manager to report to our VP of Growth. You'll own the Growth surface for one of those bets while helping build a growth-led way of working across the company.
What you’ll be doing
Own Growth for a core product area end to end, acquisition, activation, adoption and retention, baked into the roadmap from the start, not retrofitted.
Partner closely with the core product PMs and engineers who own the surface, bringing high-impact growth ideas and working out where they fit, and getting the primitives exposed that let you build and scale on top.
Design growth into the product itself: discovery-led acquisition loops, and experiences that get users to their job-to-be-done in a couple of clicks (sometimes without opening the editor at all).
Rally teams around specific, measurable outcomes and help each one hit its goal faster through what you build together.
Work across engineering, marketing and GTM to make funnel- and journey-thinking a normal part of how we build.

AI-native. You’ve driven AI into how a product or team works - not just worked somewhere that does AI. You use it daily, you’re curious about how the stack works, and you keep up as it moves (fast).
Scrappy and comfortable in ambiguity. You’ve taken something 0→1, you move fast, and you don’t need a clean brief or a stable roadmap to make progress. Constant change energises you rather than blocking you.
A builder of credibility. You win trust across teams quickly and can get engineers, PMs and GTM aligned around growth - even when that’s a new way of working for them.
Technically fluent and genuinely curious. You can hold your own with engineers on how things work and where the trade-offs are.
Outcome-driven. You anchor on the right metric and move it.

Experience as a Product Manager with exposure to Growth. Depth in a single specific lever is a plus, not a prerequisite.
Demonstrable experience driving AI-native product or ways of working.
Comfortable in a fast-moving, 0→1, frequently-disrupted environment.
Strong communication and the personality to build credibility and influence across functions.
Technical fluency to partner credibly with engineering.
Location
Remote from Europe or hybrid based from our London or Munich offices.

At Synthesia we’re passionate about building, not talking, planning or politicising. We strive to hire the smartest, kindest and most unrelenting people and let them do their best work without distractions. Our work principles serve as our charter for how we make decisions, give feedback and structure our work to empower everyone to go as fast as possible. You can find out more about these principles here.

🚀 About WRITER
WRITER is where the world's leading enterprises orchestrate AI-powered work. Our vision is to expand human capacity through superintelligence. And we're proving it's possible – through powerful, trustworthy AI that unites IT and business teams together to unlock enterprise-wide transformation.

With WRITER's end-to-end platform, hundreds of companies like Mars, Marriott, Uber, and Vanguard are building and deploying AI agents that are grounded in their company's data and fueled by WRITER's enterprise-grade LLMs.

Valued at $1.9B and backed by industry-leading investors including Premji Invest, Radical Ventures, and ICONIQ Growth, WRITER is rapidly cementing its position as the leader in enterprise generative AI.
Founded in 2020 with office hubs in San Francisco, New York City, Seattle, Austin, Chicago, and London, our team thinks big and moves fast, and we're looking for smart, hardworking builders and scalers to join us on our journey to create a better future of work with AI.

This is a chance to help shape the next chapter of WRITER's product at a moment when generative AI is redefining how work gets done. As senior staff product manager, you'll report directly to Wil Pong, VP of Product, and operate as a force-multiplier across the product organization — setting direction where it's unclear, aligning stakeholders, and making sure our most critical initiatives ship with excellence.
You'll own ambiguous, high-impact problem spaces that span multiple product areas and teams, and you'll be equal parts strategist and operator. One moment you're shaping a multi-quarter roadmap; the next you're rolling up your sleeves to unblock execution. We're looking for someone who thrives at the intersection of customer empathy, technical depth, and business judgment — and who is energized by turning complex, evolving AI capabilities into products customers love.

Drive high-impact product initiatives end-to-end, from discovery and problem definition through launch, adoption, and iteration across areas that span multiple squads and surfaces
Shape product strategy and roadmap in partnership with the VP of Product and product leadership, translating company-level goals into clear, sequenced, ambitious bets
Spend time with enterprise buyers, end users, and prospects to uncover unmet needs, validate problem-solution fit, and champion the customer voice in every decision
Partner closely with engineering and design to define requirements, navigate technical tradeoffs, and build the right things in the right order, bringing real fluency to conversations about LLMs, agents, platform architecture, and data
Align cross-functional stakeholders across go-to-market, sales, marketing, customer success, and executive leadership, communicating strategy and tradeoffs with crisp, audience-appropriate narrative
Define and own success metrics for your areas, using data and qualitative signal to evaluate impact, course-correct, and tell the story of outcomes to leadership
Raise the bar on product craft across the org by mentoring and coaching other PMs, modeling best practices, and strengthening a culture built on rigor, customer obsession, and velocity
⭐️ Is this you?
8+ years of product management experience with a track record of owning and shipping complex, high-impact products, ideally in SaaS, platform, infrastructure, or AI/ML-driven environments
Senior- or staff-level experience operating autonomously across ambiguous, multi-team problem spaces and influencing outcomes well beyond your immediate team
Genuine customer obsession — you instinctively go to the customer, synthesize signal from noise, and design from a deep understanding of real workflows and pain points
Technical credibility to engage meaningfully with engineers and researchers on system design, LLM capabilities, data, and architecture, knowing when to go deep and when to defer to the experts
A blend of strong strategic thinking and relentless execution — you can set a compelling vision one moment and sweat the details of a release plan the next
Exceptional communication that you tailor for any audience, from a frontline engineer to the executive team, driving alignment without relying on org chart authority
A mentor's instinct and a builder's drive, with the data-informed, outcome-driven mindset to define success up front and move with the speed this environment demands

Experience building products powered by LLMs, generative AI, or large-scale AI/ML systems
Background in enterprise software, developer platforms, or developer-facing products
Familiarity with AI governance, guardrails, and the operational considerations of deploying AI in regulated or high-stakes environments

About Zip
Zip is the AI platform for enterprise procurement — built for humans and agents working together. By orchestrating procurement across teams, tools, and suppliers with the help of AI agents, companies can secure the resources they need to innovate faster than ever before.
The world’s most influential enterprises trust Zip, including T-Mobile, OpenAI, AMD, Mars, Dollar Tree, and more. Together they’ve saved over $8 billion and processed over $500 billion in spend. Zip’s team includes product leaders from Apple, Airbnb, and Meta, as well as former procurement leaders from United Health, Sanofi, MGM Resorts, Discover, and NASA.
Backed by Adams Street, Alkeon, BOND, CRV, DST, Tiger Global, and Y Combinator, Zip has raised $371 million, most recently at a $2.2 billion valuation and has been recognized by Forbes Fintech 50, Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies, Inc. Best in Business, and LinkedIn Top Startups.
Please note we are looking for someone who is willing and able to come into our downtown San Francisco office on a hybrid basis (3 days / week).

We're hiring a Senior/Principal Product Manager (experience dependent) to lead Zip's Contract Orchestration product, one of the company's newest and most strategic bets. Buy-side contracting is still broken: reviews and redlines live in email threads, signed agreements disappear into shared drives, and requesters call the process a black box.

Zip's customers execute over a million contract reviews a year and most of them are routine agreements. We just launched AI Contract Orchestration to take that work off legal and procurement, and there is far more to build.
You'll own the vision and strategy for one or more areas of this product, end to end and with a high degree of autonomy.

The category is established, but Zip has an edge: as the front door for procurement, we see every contract with clean intake data on the requester, spend, category, and risk, so our AI can review clauses, propose redlines, and route work on real context rather than the document alone.

As PM, you'll balance different users' interests throughout the contracting process (procurement, legal, finance, requesters, suppliers), and you'll own the quality bar that lets legal trust AI with language that carries real liability.
You Will
Set the vision and multi-quarter strategy for Contract Orchestration, with a clear, opinionated view of where we beat incumbent CLMs
Ship AI that does the work: clause analysis, playbook-grounded redlines, contract generation, triage and routing, and metadata extraction accurate enough to trust
Own the full lifecycle, from intake and negotiation to the repository, contract families, renewals, and contract-to-spend compliance
Work directly with customers to ship features that reduce contract cycle times and increase contract visibility and compliance
Build agents and own the AI quality bar end to end: evals, guardrails, and feedback loops
Roll up your sleeves wherever the team needs it, from user research to reviewing extraction quality on a customer's contracts

4 - 8+ years of Product Management experience, preferably in B2B SaaS, owning ambiguous, high-impact areas end to end
Deep experience partnering with engineering and design to ship sophisticated products with a great user experience
Experience with workflow or document-heavy enterprise products
A track record of setting product strategy and influencing cross-functional partners and leadership without direct authority
Experience shipping AI or ML features where accuracy is non-negotiable, including how you measured and improved quality
Strong written and verbal communication with internal and external stakeholders, including executives
Extreme attention to detail, with the ability to quickly grasp complex business processes and industry knowledge
Ability to prioritize ruthlessly, even if it may disappoint customers or stakeholders

About Chartis
The challenges facing US healthcare are longstanding and all too familiar. We are Chartis, and we believe in better. About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

As Claude reaches more people, including individuals, businesses, developers building on our APIs, and the platforms and resellers building on top of those, knowing who is on the other side of a request and what they are allowed to do becomes foundational to running our products responsibly. Creating a centralized identity, verification, and access system that every Claude surface draws on is important to accomplishing our mission.
We are hiring a Product Manager to own the safe access. The primitives are the building blocks the rest of Anthropic uses to manage access to models and capabilities: access programs, accounts, organization linking, verifications, user APIs for platforms, and the internal tooling teams use. You will own the end-to-end product experience and strategy for internal and external access,, across every surface.
This is a role for a strong executor with the ability to be agile in shipping in a 0-1 product space. Safe access is a new product that sits on the critical path of every model launch and every access program. Requirements arrive from many organizations at once, and most weeks you will be the person defining the problem rather than receiving it.

Own the product strategy and roadmap for the account and access primitives, with the goal that any team at Anthropic can provision access or run an access program with minimal support. This is highly ambiguous and requires a lot of cross team coordination and deep understanding of the systems of today.
Own the end-to-end experience of getting and managing access for internal stakeholders (research, model launches, safeguards, go-to-market) and for external customers and partners, and keep it consistent across every surface. This requires thinking through many user types, with vastly different experiences.
Support the API designs and the UX of the access APIs that platforms, resellers, and internal services integrate with. Work through the designs with engineering and make calls on the primitives yourself.
Partner with the trusted access and verification product managers so that new programs compose from shared primitives rather than one-off builds.
Coordinate across the product, safeguards, legal, and go-to-market teams, and drive alignment when their requirements conflict.

Are a strong executor with a track record of shipping through ambiguity and cross-organization dependencies.
Write clearly enough that an engineer, an executive, and an external partner can each see the tradeoff you are making.
Have owned a developer platform, identity, authorization, or access-management product end to end, and were the person accountable for its outcomes (for most people this means five or more years as a PM, but we care about the ownership, not the years).
Care about Anthropic's mission, and specifically about scaling access to Claude safely.

Built account, identity, or subscription systems that span more than one product

How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles.

We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

We're looking for a Lead Product Manager to lead the Banners team, which owns Braze's in-product messaging surfaces: Content Cards and Banners.
These are the channels that reach users inside the app experience rather than outside it. They're persistent, native, and always available, with no opt-in required and no deliverability tax. Content Cards is a mature, widely adopted surface. Banners is our newest channel and our fastest growing, having gone from launch to full feature parity with Content Cards in under a year, and now serving well over a billion impressions a day.
Braze operates at massive scale, collecting hundreds of billions of data points each month and sending billions of messages to end users daily. In-product surfaces are a growing share of that. The constraint on this part of the business is no longer capability. It's adoption, programmability, and making creation genuinely fast.
The goal here is to find someone who can take a portfolio that's technically deep and commercially material, and push it into its next phase. Here's what you'd focus on in your first year:
Drive adoption, not just delivery. The work is turning shipped capability into activated customers and sustained usage. That means better defaults, faster time to first banner, self-serve setup, and out-of-the-box integrations with platforms like Shopify
Make creation faster and more intelligent. Banners already supports three ways to build: drag-and-drop, raw HTML, and AI-generated. Braze is investing heavily in Operator, our AI assistant, and a big part of this role is making sure these surfaces are ones Operator can actually work with.

Marketers are shifting from building things themselves to letting AI build it for them. A core part of this role is pushing that path forward: making Operator, our AI assistant, a natural and differentiated way to act on a marketer’s intent
Make these surfaces first-class programmable products. You'd drive REST API parity, translations support, enterprise-grade access scoping, and the path to serving in-product content over a public API without an SDK dependency
Own hard technical product work at scale. Render latency at the 99th percentile, the SDK dependencies these surfaces sit on top of, unifying the technical foundation for these channels–in this role, product judgment and technical judgment are the same judgment
Set the measurement bar. You'd define what good looks like for adoption, usage, and performance, and hold the team to baselines and targets that are real

Define and own the roadmap for Content Cards and Banners, pulling from customers, sales, support, usage data, and competitive signal to figure out what matters most next
Partner with engineers and designers to execute that roadmap in a lean, entrepreneurial start-up environment
Own the commercial outcomes for your area (adoption, consumption, expansion) and understand the unit economics well enough to make good investment tradeoffs
Establish and manage internal and external customer expectations, including with enterprise accounts and in renewal and expansion conversations
Deeply understand our technology, business, customers, and market
Build best-in-class infrastructure for your products, treating reliability, performance, and observability as product requirements rather than cleanup work
Partner across the division to build reusable capability instead of channel-specific implementations. Shared editors, shared design patterns, shared APIs

8+ years of Product Management experience, including owning a product line at scale

Braze produces content across dozens of products, teams, and markets. Localizing that content today runs through Phrase and a set of manual processes that, while functional, create bottlenecks that don't add proportional value. We're building an AI-powered translation infrastructure to change that; we need a TPM who can own it.

This is an early-stage platform role. The architecture is taking shape; the problems aren't all known yet. You'll be most effective if you thrive in that ambiguity.You'll sit on the Content Platforms team as a senior individual contributor.

No direct reports, but a strong remit to lead — setting direction, raising the bar, and pulling colleagues across teams toward better solutions.You'll design systems that let teams self-serve and drive the technical execution of an internal AI translation platform.

AI won't replace human judgment in this process — you'll help us figure out where human review is essential and design workflows that make that review fast, targeted, and high-quality. The goal is to remove friction that doesn't need to exist, not to cut corners on quality.

Localization at Braze touches almost every part of the business: Demand Gen, Product Marketing, Sales, Enablement, Product, Engineering, Support, and the regional teams that depend on locally-relevant content to do their jobs.

Your first job is to plug into the existing localization program — understand what's working, what's not, and where the people closest to it think the real opportunities are. The platform we build has to be informed by that reality, not imposed on it.This is not a research role and it's not a presentations role.

You'll write code, ship prototypes, pair with engineers, and measure adoption. AI-assisted development is how we work — you'll be expected to use it, build with it, and be opinionated about it.
Room To Grow
The role itself is Senior TPM, Content Platforms — the parenthetical reflects initial focus, not permanent scope. The team owns a broader technical content operations remit, and as the localization platform matures we expect this role to expand into adjacent problem areas. The right candidate sees localization as a way in, not the whole job.
Why This Role Matters For You
The localization industry is in the middle of a real shift, and most people in it are watching from the sidelines.

This role puts you at the front of it — not as someone reacting to AI, but as someone deciding how an enterprise actually adopts it.You'll build the kind of experience that compounds: hands-on systems thinking, real product ownership, and fluency with the tools that are reshaping how technical work gets done.

A problem big enough to matter, the autonomy to shape the solution, and a team of engineers who actually want to build with you.This is a role for people who'd rather shape how AI gets used than watch it happen to them.

Own the localization infrastructure product: roadmap, architecture decisions, stakeholder alignment
Partner with engineers to design and ship multi-platform systems that meet complex, evolving localization needs across the business
Build functional prototypes independently to validate ideas and sharpen requirements before full engineering investment
Design the workflows and self-serve patterns that let teams move forward without routing every request through a central queue
Drive adoption of AI-assisted translation tooling while maintaining quality and consistency standards
Help us make smart build-vs-buy decisions — knowing when to build internal tooling and when existing or emerging vendors are the better answer
Manage relationships with translation and localization vendors — what we expect of them, what we move away from, and how their work integrates with everything we build

PMs are encouraged to apply, but so are solutions architects, solutions consultants, engineers, and others with a background in localization or content operations. Read the rest as a description of the work, not a checklist of prior titles.
Localization Background
A working background in localization is a strong plus, but it isn't a requirement. What we do need is a thoughtful interest in the space — someone who has read into the problem, has views on where AI shifts the cost curve, and is genuinely curious about how a modern enterprise should be running this kind of program. If you bring the systems thinking and product instincts, we can build the domain depth around you.
If you do have localization experience, here's what we'd expect you to bring:
Familiar with the localization landscape — tools, workflows, vendor relationships, and where the real friction lives
Able to develop a clear framework for when human review is required, tuned to content type, audience, risk, and context — not just an instinct, but a defensible model others can apply
Experience with platforms like Phrase is relevant context
Technical foundation
Deeply familiar with headless CMS architecture; Sanity experience is a strong plus
Comfortable with Node.js, TypeScript, and modern web frameworks
Able to build simple web apps and functional prototypes on your own — you won't be shipping complex systems to production solo, but you can independently validate an idea end-to-end
Comfortable building with AI development tools like Claude Code or Cursor
Product Instincts
Comfortable architecting multi-platform systems and reasoning about long-term design tradeoffs
Truly embedded with engineering — not just mediating through tickets and grooming sessions, but collaborating in real time, pairing on problems, and helping the team move faster using the AI development tools available today
Can hold your own in technical conversations without needing to defer every decision
Experienced managing stakeholders across team boundaries, including customers who have real expectations tied to your delivery
Mindset
Genuinely curious about what AI makes possible — not as a buzzword, but as a tool you use and build with

We are hiring a Product Manager to join our AI & App Experience (AAX) team, with a focus on design systems. In this role, you’ll help shape the shared foundations that make it easier for teams across Chime to build consistent, intuitive, and high-quality member experiences.
You’ll own product strategy and execution for design-system capabilities that sit at the intersection of product, design, and engineering. You’ll work across teams to understand where fragmented patterns, tooling, and workflows create friction, then turn those insights into scalable systems that improve both the quality of our app experience and the speed at which teams can build it.
The base salary offered for this role and level of experience will begin at $196,000 and up to $255,000. Full-time employees are also eligible for a bonus, competitive equity package, and benefits. The actual base salary offered may be higher, depending on your location, skills, qualifications, and experience.
In this role, you can expect to
Own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for design-system capabilities within AAX, connecting platform investments to meaningful improvements in Chime’s member experience.
Partner closely with Design and Engineering to evolve shared components, patterns, tooling, and infrastructure that enable teams to build cohesive app experiences more efficiently.
Identify high-leverage opportunities to improve how product teams discover, adopt, and contribute to Chime’s design system, balancing consistency with the flexibility teams need to innovate.
Develop a deep understanding of the needs of internal product builders and translate those needs into clear product priorities, requirements, and measurable outcomes.
Drive alignment across multiple product areas, helping teams make thoughtful tradeoffs when shared platform needs, individual product needs, and longer-term experience quality intersect.
Establish success measures for the design system, using quantitative and qualitative signals to understand adoption, developer and designer effectiveness, experience consistency, and business impact.
Help define how emerging AI capabilities can improve the way Chime teams design, build, and maintain app experiences, where relevant to the design-system strategy.
To thrive in this role, you have
8+ years of experience as a Product Manager.
Product management experience owning complex products, platforms, or internal systems from strategy through execution in a technology environment.
Experience working on design systems, developer platforms, UI frameworks, shared product infrastructure, or similarly horizontal capabilities used by multiple teams.
A track record of translating ambiguous, cross-functional problems into a clear product strategy, prioritized roadmap, and measurable outcomes.
Experience partnering deeply with Product Design and Engineering, with enough technical and design fluency to navigate component architecture, platform constraints, user experience tradeoffs, and implementation decisions.
Experience driving adoption of a shared product or platform across multiple teams, including identifying user pain points and influencing stakeholders without relying on direct authority.
Evidence of using data, research, and customer or internal-user feedback to prioritize investments and assess whether a product or platform is delivering meaningful value.
Experience operating in environments where quality, consistency, scale, and speed all matter, and where product decisions require balancing near-term delivery with durable foundations.

At Chime, we believe in the power of our product to help people lead healthier financial lives. The Trust & Safety team is tasked with keeping our members’ accounts safe, providing them uninterrupted access to their money, and minimizing the company’s risk exposure and fraud loss.
We are looking for a Product Manager to lead product strategy and execution for Transaction Risk Decisioning at Chime .
This team builds the decisioning systems and product experiences that help Chime evaluate transaction risk in real time across card payments, peer-to-peer payments, bank transfers, and other money movement surfaces. The team partners closely with engineering, analytics, risk strategy, operations, and platform teams to reduce fraud, improve approval rates, and make risk outcomes clearer and more recoverable for members.
For our members, this space is deeply personal. A risk decision can determine whether a card transaction goes through, whether money movement succeeds, whether a suspicious action is stopped in time, and whether a member feels protected or unfairly blocked. The best products in this area make safety visible without making everyday banking harder. They keep friction targeted to risky behavior, not normal behavior, and turn declines or interventions into understandable, recoverable experiences.
What this team owns
This is a high-leverage role at the intersection of risk, growth, trust, and product quality. The team owns outbound transaction risk across card authorization, ACH, peer-to-peer, outbound transfers, and related surfaces — protecting a large share of Chime's revenue while minimizing fraud and disputes and enabling healthy growth.
In this role, you can expect to
Drive strategy to reduce transaction declines and increase purchase volume authorization rates — directly impacting members' experience with Chime, and helping Chime's revenue and purchase volume growth
Launch new controls for an emerging fraud pattern across a money movement rail
Redesign a risky decline flow so more good members recover successfully while bad actors are still contained,
Work cross functionally with analysts, data science, Compliance, Legal and engineers to improve the quality of risk signals flowing into a decision checkpoint,
Partner with member support teams to make a confusing risk outcome understandable and actionable for members,
Help launch new financial products safely by designing the right safeguards, fallbacks, and monitoring.
To thrive in this role, you have
5+ years of experience as a Product Manager
Deep expertise in payments risk — you understand how card networks operate, including Visa and Mastercard transaction rules, authorization reason codes, dispute and chargeback frameworks, and decline return codes (e.g., Do Not Honor, Insufficient Funds, Card Activity Limit). You can hold a substantive conversation with a risk strategist, a network partner, or an issuer processor about why a transaction declined and what can be done about it
Proven ability to think strategically about purchase volume and authorization rates , you've connected decisioning logic to revenue outcomes and can frame risk tradeoffs in terms of business impact, not just fraud loss
A track record of bringing thought leadership to hard, ambiguous problems - you don't just execute on a roadmap, you shape it. You can articulate a compelling vision for how the transaction experience should work and build alignment across engineering, risk, compliance, and leadership
A strong product mindset and the ability to translate complex risk and platform challenges into clear strategy and execution
Experience operating in systems with significant policy, operational, and data dependencies
The ability to engage fluently across member journeys, policy behavior, experiment design, and platform capabilities
Strong customer empathy and a track record of turning user insights into product decisions — with a particular sensitivity to how declines and friction moments affect member trust and retention
Strong analytical skills and experience applying machine learning and AI methodologies
Deep curiosity and a strong sense of ownership
Experience working in a fast-growing, cross-functional environment
A passion for helping members lead healthy financial lives

At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies.

Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request.

As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.
At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools.

Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up.

If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.
Available Locations: London, Lisbon, or New York

As a Senior Product Manager for Application Protection & Governance, you’ll join our core Application Security team to protect web, API applications against evolving abuse and threat patterns. You will own the product outcomes that help customers deploy, operate, and improve security controls over time, turning complex security requirements into practical capabilities and operational guidance.
In this role, you will partner with engineering, security specialists and the go-to-market organization to define product direction and drive adoption across areas including web, LLM and API protection (for example, profiling and validation of traffic patterns, schema-aware enforcement, and reducing risks from interconnected third- and fourth-party integrations).

You’ll also establish measurement and feedback loops to assess effectiveness, reduce customer operational friction, and continuously iterate based on real-world results.
You’ll be the strategic anchor for these initiatives aligning customer needs, internal safety requirements, and technical feasibility to deliver reliable protection for applications at global scale.

End-to-End Product Ownership: Own the entire user journey for your product portfolio, ensuring a seamless experience across both programmatic APIs and user-facing dashboards (UX). Collaborate closely with design teams to build intuitive, developer-friendly interfaces.
Roadmap & Strategy: Deeply understand the application security landscape and analyze customer pain points to define, prioritize, and own the product roadmap.
Voice of the Customer: Meet regularly with customers and partners to gather direct feedback, understand real-world deployment challenges, and continuously inject customer insights back into the product lifecycle.
Iterative Execution: Partner with engineering and the broader application security organization to ship impactful features. At Cloudflare, we are biased for action, we prioritize shipping early, gathering data, and iterating rapidly.
Go-to-Market & Documentation: Own all customer-facing communications and technical documentation, ensuring complex security features are easily understood and adopted by our users.
Cross-Functional Leadership: Serve as the primary point of contact for your products, both internally and externally.
Sales & Support Enablement: Actively support the sales organization across all stages of customer engagement (pre-sales strategy and post-sales expansion and adoption). Collaborate tightly with Customer Support to resolve technical issues and incidents.

Proven Product Management Experience: 4+ years of experience as a Product Manager successfully delivering high-scale cloud solutions targeted at a technical audience within the B2B SaaS industry.
Customer Focus: Ability to design for massive enterprises without compromising the experience for individual developers and small businesses. You excel at balancing the diverse needs of Cloudflare's broad user base.
Deep Technical Acumen: Comfortable engaging in deep technical discussions with engineering teams. You can quickly grasp complex security concepts and translate them into clear, compelling narratives for customers through blog posts, whitepapers, and direct calls.
AI-Driven Productivity: Embrace and actively adopt advanced AI tools to work autonomously, streamline product management workflows, and maximize efficiency to ship high-quality products faster.
Preferred Experience: Professional background in web security, API security, application security, or cloud security infrastructure is highly preferred.

As a Senior Product Manager at Cloudflare, you will be responsible for building products that improve the way that the Internet works. Product Managers at Cloudflare shape high-level product goals but also get our hands dirty. On an average day, you might pitch a concept to senior leadership, collaborate with marketing, conduct user research, prototype a new feature, iterate on a spec, analyze usage data, and pair with an engineer on implementation.

As the product manager for Organization and Partner Experiences, you will be responsible for building the management plane that helps everyone, but especially enterprises and partners like resellers, MSSPs, and OEMs scale their use of Cloudflare across multiple accounts. This is a deeply collaborative role which requires a healthy blend of technical background, user experience, and business savvy. You will:
Own your space. You will own the priorities and scope for a high performing engineering team focusing on building the Organizations management plane at Cloudflare.
Connect the pieces. Product managers are a nerve center at Cloudflare, responsible for connecting engineering, program management, marketing, revenue, and partners to make sure that our ships go out on time and with the maximum impact.
Excel across teams. Enterprise capabilities cut across all of our product verticals, so you should be comfortable working with product managers across the company to prioritize systemic improvements that our enterprise customers need.
Be customer obsessed. You will be responsible for directly engaging with customers and understanding how they use our products. You’ll bring these insights back to the team to build a great roadmap.
Be data driven. You should be comfortable working with data, and analyzing data to quantify the impact of problems and opportunities in your space.

6+ years of experience as a product manager, technical program manager, or equivalent delivering solutions in the cloud at scale for a technical audience
Customer focus. At Cloudflare, we serve the needs of customers large and small, and our product managers need to be comfortable understanding how to design for enterprises without compromising the experience for individuals and small businesses.
User experience sense. You’re comfortable working with product designers to translate the requirements into an elegant user experience.
Enterprise sense. You’ve worked on products that are for enterprises, and know what they need to be competitive in today’s environment.
Strong written and verbal communication skills for both an internal and external audience as appropriate.

You’ve enthusiastically adopted the latest generation of agentic coding tools, and you can use them effectively to navigate a codebase, or prototype the improvements you envision for your feature area.
Partners - You’ve worked closely with go to market partners or resellers and understand how to build products that make them more effective
Data-fluency - Can you work directly with data yourself to build confidence in your views and can you use that same data to persuade others?
At Cloudflare it’s pretty helpful to understand how the Internet really works at layers 2 through 7. If you don’t have this, be prepared to speak with mastery about another realm of similar complexity.

As a Product Manager – Code Intelligence , you will define, build, and launch capabilities that proactively detect infrastructure issues in code (e.g. Terraform, Helm) and recommend changes before they can be deployed into production and escalate into production incidents. We are looking for a Lead Product Manager to join the Patient Profile team in the Patient domain.
Your mission will be to make the patient health record complete, accurate and current enough that everything else we build can act on it, the health recommendations, care plans and assistant experiences that help people take their health into their own hands. You will work in a feature team developing the Patient Health Record, health trackers, patient account and online identity, contributing directly to the quality of the medical support we provide to both patients and practitioners.
A patient record is built from four channels: what patients enter themselves, what they share when preparing a consultation, what we retrieve from health professionals' systems, and what they connect from third-party sources such as Apple Health, Google Health Connect and national health record services.

Three of those channels belong to teams you will not manage. You will own the outcome across all four, the most leveraged place to sit in a health platform, and only reachable through other people.
You will also work inside a hard regulatory perimeter: health data, GDPR, consent by design.

s.h: Your responsibilities include but are not limited to
s.t:
Own the end-to-end patient data collection programme across every channel a patient record is built from, and be accountable for the result across all four
Define what a useful record actually means for the teams that depend on it, make that definition measurable, and instrument it rather than inheriting a dashboard
Partner with the channel-owning teams inside and outside the group: set the inter-team contracts, agree how each channel contributes, and arbitrate collection priorities
Own record quality and freshness rather than volume, alongside health data storage consent, patient account and online identity
Ship the layers that serve this data to the rest of the product: the patient feature store, the patient context service and the Patient Health Record feature
Lead the Patient Profile team's roadmap and delivery, from PHR (patient health record) and trackers through to the feature store and context service
Before you read on: if you don't have the exact profile described below, but you feel this job description matches your skill set, we still encourage you to apply.

s.h: You'll be a great fit if you
s.t:
You have owned a coverage, completeness or data quality metric as your primary objective, and can say what it went from, to what, and over how long
You have worked at millions-of-records scale
You have moved that metric through teams that did not report to you, setting interfaces, contracts and SLAs with partner teams
You have shipped under a hard regulatory or consent constraint, in health, finance or identity, with privacy and consent by design
You have real technical depth: you have owned a data platform component as a product, a feature store, a context or profile service, or an identity layer.
You are fluent in English

s.h: It would be fantastic if you
s.t:
You have had a data quality problem surface only once it reached a downstream consumer, and you changed how you worked because of it
You have built a completeness or quality definition and made an organisation adopt it
You have worked on interoperability, health data standards, or identity and account models

Execute with urgency and excellence

We're looking for a Principal Product Manager to be the primary product voice for Elastic Security's most strategic enterprise customers. Solid products are built on a clear knowledge of real customer needs. In large enterprise accounts, those needs arrive as a constant stream of enhancement requests, feature asks, and hard problems.

They often arrive faster than any one team can act on them. Someone has to bring order to that stream, tell apart what a customer wants from what a customer needs, and turn it into a coherent product direction across different product areas.
In this high-impact role, you will own the relationship between Elastic Security's product organization and our most strategic enterprise accounts. You will manage enhancement requests across many enterprise customers at once.

You will prioritize them with judgment and data, and make sure they keep transitioning through the system instead of sitting idle.

You will be the person a CISO trusts in the room, the person an engineering lead respects for the quality of your requirements, and the person who can tell a major customer that something will not be built without losing the relationship.

You will work at the intersection of Product, Sales, Customer Success, and Engineering, building the structure that lets Elastic scale close customer relationships without simply adding headcount.
What You Will Be Doing
Own the enhancement request pipeline across multiple strategic enterprise accounts at once. Build and maintain a structured system to track, prioritize, and respond to customer-sourced requirements, and keep requests moving rather than leaving them in “under consideration.”
Translate customer requirements into shipped products. Work at the level of customer pain, not just the feature that was asked for, and synthesize input from many accounts into a single, coherent product direction.
Turn input from strategic accounts into successful products. Look for patterns across accounts. Shape some of these patterns into formal partnerships for design. Make sure the resulting capabilities benefit the wider market, not just the single customer that made the request.
Feed validated customer patterns back into the core product roadmaps, influencing direction well beyond the accounts you cover.
Serve as the primary product voice in meetings with senior customer stakeholders, including the CISO, CTO, and VP of Security Operations. Deliver roadmap updates, including deprioritizations and misses, in a way that keeps the relationship deep.
Prioritize customer-sourced requirements using structured frameworks such as RICE, weighted scoring, and opportunity sizing. Use data where it is available and clear judgment where it is thin, and be transparent about which is which.
Partner with product and engineering leads to write requirements they can act on without follow-up clarification meetings. Understand system architecture well enough to assess feasibility and scope on your own.
Operate across Product, Sales, Customer Success, and Legal. Support deal cycles as a product resource through RFP responses, security questionnaires, and roadmap presentations to prospects.
Navigate tension between a customer's contractual expectations and the internal roadmap , and tackle it directly rather than through routine escalation.
Create artifacts such as roadmap trackers, enhancement request dashboards, and decision memos that give customers and internal stakeholders visibility without requiring a meeting.
Advocate for customer needs inside the company while resisting the pull of the loudest or largest customer setting the roadmap at the expense of the broader market.

Extensive Experience: 7–10 years of product management experience, with at least 4 years in B2B enterprise software. A consistent record of owning a product area with meaningful revenue impact and of leading products from customer input through shipped, iterated outcomes. Direct experience working with named strategic accounts, not only through customer success proxies. Experience with hyperscalers, MSSPs and/or PubSec is a solid plus.
Security Domain Knowledge: Hands-on knowledge with SIEM, SOAR, XDR or broader security operations platforms, either as a product manager or as a practitioner such as a SOC analyst, detection engineer, or security architect.

You can credibly discuss detection engineering, log ingestion pipelines, correlation rules, threat hunting workflows, and compliance use cases without a solutions engineer in the room. You understand the difference between what a CISO wants to hear and what a SOC analyst actually needs.

A background as a security practitioner, such as SOC, incident response, or detection engineering, before moving into product is a solid plus, and brings credibility that is hard to teach.
Enhancement Request Management at Scale: You have personally run a structured enhancement request pipeline across several enterprise accounts at the same time. You can step into a relationship with dozens of open requests and no prior documentation and build a working tracking system within weeks.
Executive Presence: You are comfortable as the primary product voice with C-suite and VP-level customer stakeholders. You can deliver difficult news without losing the relationship, and you can hold both the executive view and the analyst view in the same meeting.
Technical Credibility: You earn respect from engineering through the quality of your requirements rather than through authority. You write specs engineers can act on, and you know enough about architecture to judge feasibility and scope.
Cross-functional Leadership and Influence: You have operated at the intersection of Product, Sales, Customer Success, Engineering, and Legal, and you know which function owns what and how to advance work across all of them. You lead across a matrixed organization, align multiple stakeholders toward a common vision, and drive execution in a dynamic, remote-first environment, with the autonomy and judgment expected of a principal-level product leader.
Structured Thinking and Bias for Closure: You bring order to unstructured problems, using data to prioritize and clear judgment when data is thin, and staying transparent about which is which. You move work through the system and follow up proactively rather than waiting to be asked, defaulting to visibility through artifacts instead of meetings. You advocate for customer needs while synthesizing them into product direction rather than relaying demands.

Elastic Security is looking for a Senior Product Manager to help build and grow Elastic XDR. Great detection-and-response products come from a clear read of how attacks unfold and where defenders lose time, and this role puts you close to both. You will own a core area of the XDR roadmap end to end, from requirements through shipped, iterated product, and contribute to the exposure and vulnerability capabilities now converging with it.
You will be the person an engineering lead respects for the quality of your requirements, and a credible product voice in front of security customers. You will work on a platform whose unified data model and deployment flexibility, from cloud to on-premises to fully air-gapped, , partnering closely with Engineering and the Elastic Security Labs research team. This is a role for a product manager ready to own meaningful surface area in a fast-moving space and grow toward broader ownership.
What You Will Be Doing
Own a core area of the XDR roadmap end to end: drive detection, correlation, incident building, and response capabilities across endpoint, cloud, identity, and network, from requirements through shipped and iterated product.
Expand and maintain the telemetry and integrations XDR depends on: first-party Elastic data plus third-party EDR, cloud, identity, and network sources that let the product correlate across a real environment.
Contribute to Elastic's exposure and vulnerability management work, including prioritization based on exploitability and reachability rather than raw CVSS, and remediation workflow.
Write requirements engineering can act on without follow-up clarification meetings, and translate customer input and threat research from Elastic Security Labs into product.
Represent product in customer conversations, including senior security stakeholders, and bring what you learn back into the roadmap .
Ensure your capabilities work across Elastic's deployment models, from cloud to on-premises to air-gapped, so they hold up in regulated and disconnected environments.
Maintain well-developed awareness of the competitive landscape and GTM strategies.
Create artifacts such as roadmap trackers and decision memos that give stakeholders visibility without requiring a meeting.

Experience: At least 5 years in security-related technical product management, competitive analysis, or technical marketing, and a minimum of 3 years in a related product development or technical field. A track record of owning product areas from requirements through shipped, iterated outcomes.
Detection and Response Domain Knowledge: Hands-on knowledge of XDR, EDR, SIEM, incident response, or forensic either as a product manager or as a practitioner such as a SOC analyst, detection engineer, or incident responder. You can discuss correlation, response, and detection engineering credibly. A practitioner background before transitioning into product is a solid plus.
Telemetry and Integration Breadth: Comfort building or owning products that rely on heterogeneous third-party data, with a awareness that XDR depends on ingestion breadth and healthy integrations.
Analytics and Threat Understanding: A solid comprehension of the analytics techniques behind detection and prioritization and of the current cyber threat landscape. Familiarity with AI security, how AI, ML, and agentic systems are attacked and defended, is a plus. Solid comprehension is required; hands-on modeling is not.
Technical Credibility: You earn respect from engineering through the quality of your requirements, and you know enough about architecture to judge feasibility and scope.
Customer-Facing Confidence: You are comfortable representing product to security customers, including senior stakeholders, and can hold both the practitioner and the leadership view in the same conversation.
Communication Excellence: You can distill complex detection engineering and exposure concepts into clear narratives for both technical and non-technical audiences.
Comfortable with AI-Augmented Work: You use AI tooling for synthesis, research, and delivery as a regular part of your workflow, and you own the final outcomes regardless of how they were produced.
Cross-functional Collaboration: You have operated across Product, Engineering, Sales, and Customer Success, and you drive execution in a dynamic, remote-first environment with growing autonomy.
Proficiency and Education: A robust interest in cybersecurity and its challenges is essential. Attention to detail is important. You must also have the ability to understand the bigger picture. A BS or MS degree in engineering, computer science, or information security is required.

Hey there!
We’re Fever , the world’s leading tech platform for culture and live entertainment.
Our mission? To democratize access to culture and entertainment. With our proprietary cutting-edge technology and data-driven approach, we’re revolutionizing the way people engage with live entertainment.
Every month, our platform inspires over 300 million people in +55 countries (and counting) to discover unforgettable experiences while also empowering event creators with our data and technology, helping them scale, innovate, and enhance their events to reach new audiences.
Our results? We’ve teamed up with major industry leaders like Netflix, F.C. Barcelona, and Primavera Sound, presented international award-winning experiences, and are backed by several leading global investors! Impressive, right?
To achieve our mission, we are looking for bar-raisers with a hands-on mindset who are eager to help shape the future of entertainment!
Ready to be part of the experience?
Now, let’s discuss this role and what you will do to help achieve Fever’s mission.
Behind the user-friendly iOS and Android apps and webpage that work across the world is the engineering team. We are in charge of creating, developing, improving, and maintaining all Fever services so that more people can have an amazing experience.

We are now opening a new frontier: China . To lead this expansion from a product standpoint, we're looking for a Senior Product Manager based in China who deeply understands the local market, users, and digital ecosystem, and who can act as the on-the-ground product lead for Fever's entry and growth in the country, working in close daily collaboration with our global Product organization based in Madrid.
This is a founding-team-style role: you'll be shaping not just features, but how Fever shows up in China from day one.

Own the product vision and roadmap for Fever's China market entry, grounded in first-hand knowledge of local users, competitors, and market dynamics.
Act as Fever's local product voice, gathering market intelligence, user insight, and partner feedback directly from the Chinese ecosystem and channelling it into product decisions.
Break down broad market-entry opportunities into concrete, measurable, sequenced actions.
Analyze product and market performance, hypothesize, test, and continuously improve product metrics with a China-specific lens.
Develop product features from ideation to release, factoring in local payment methods, super-app integrations (WeChat, Alipay), and regulatory requirements specific to China.
Build local partnerships and relationships (venues, promoters, platforms) that inform and unlock product opportunities.
Build and communicate a compelling vision and go-to-market strategy for Fever in China, gathering support from both local stakeholders and global leadership.
Serve as the primary point of expertise on China-specific product, partnership, regulatory, and localization decisions.

Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related field.
5+ years of relevant experience in product management, with meaningful exposure to the Chinese consumer tech or entertainment/ticketing landscape.
High proficiency in Mandarin Chinese and high proficiency in business English (both mandatory), as you'll work daily with a China-based ecosystem and a Madrid-based global team.

At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year.
The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.
The Opportunity
As a Senior Product Manager at Flexport, you'll set the strategic vision and shape products that transform global logistics at scale. You’ll collaborate seamlessly with engineering, design, operations, and business teams to develop and iterate on solutions that power seamless, efficient movement of goods worldwide. Your leadership will guide the team to deliver products that empower businesses—large and small—to meet customer demands and succeed in global markets.
Omnichannel Fulfillment at Flexport

As Senior Product Manager, you'll lead the vision and execution for outbound fulfillment solutions, enabling fast and reliable deliveries for shoppers, driving innovation in an interconnected supply chain ecosystem for our merchants —and shaping the future of global trade. Lead Product Strategy: Define the holistic vision, goals, and roadmap for outbound fulfillment products supporting Flexport’s Omnichannel business lines.

Partner Cross-Functionally: Work closely with engineering, design, operations, and data science teams to establish priorities, deliver scalable, impactful solutions.
Champion Customer Insights: Gather and synthesize feedback from users, partners, and market research to inform product direction and prioritization.
Mentor and Inspire: Provide guidance and mentorship to junior product managers, fostering a culture of collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Shape the Platform: Act as a key stakeholder in defining and evolving Flexport’s Omnichannel product vision and strategy.
Drive Results: Measure product performance and iterate on features to maximize impact and business value.

Change the way the world travels
Join the GetYourGuide journey to connect people with unforgettable travel experiences around the world. Millions look to us for unique activities they can trust, and it’s all powered by our commitment to make every single journey extraordinary - including yours.
Ready to unlock your potential with a community of fellow explorers? Find your next role at our Berlin HQ or one of our local offices around the globe, from New York to Bangkok. Head to getyourguide.careers to take the first step.
Team mission
Landing pages are one of GetYourGuide's most important product surfaces — the moment where acquisition meets experience, and where the quality of what we build directly determines whether a visitor becomes a customer.

As Lead Product Manager for Landing Pages, you will own a high-traffic surface that sits at the intersection of growth, acquisition, and user experience. You will work closely with paid search, paid media, and SEO stakeholders to ensure the pages you build perform across channels, while keeping the traveller's needs at the centre of every decision. Your cross-functional team includes engineers, designers, analysts, and researchers.
This is a role for someone who thinks in systems, is energised by the product-marketing boundary, and wants to build something that scales — not just ship features. The work has direct visibility into how GetYourGuide grows, and the decisions made here have a measurable impact on the business from day one.
We are looking for a Lead PM who brings both strategic clarity and executional rigour — someone who can set a vision, bring stakeholders along, and deliver.

Build modular, reusable infrastructure — page templates, content modules, and page logic — that compounds in value over time. You are not optimising individual features; you are building the foundation that makes everything that follows faster and cheaper.
Develop and implement a strategy for your product area, set clear measurable goals, and take full responsibility for outcomes. Connect your roadmap to the company's mission, break it into actionable steps, and create genuine excitement for the long-term vision — with your team, across functions, and with executive leadership.
Apply your understanding of acquisition channel economics and how landing page content drives channel performance. Partner closely with paid search, paid media, and SEO stakeholders to ensure pages serve channel needs without being built around any single one. Hold user experience and channel performance goals together rather than trading them off.
Design and own an experimentation system at scale — not just individual A/B tests, but the architecture and cadence that enables rapid, parallel testing across page types and channels. Build toward a model that increases the speed and independence of experimentation over time.
Use customer feedback, market trends, and business metrics to drive decisions. Prioritise ruthlessly, re-evaluate the roadmap as new insights arrive, and make clear calls on sequencing to maximise both impact and learning.
Represent customer interests at all levels of the organisation. Act with openness and transparency with your team, peers, and leadership. Coach and mentor team members, foster a culture of continuous improvement, and bring others along on the vision.
Your toolkit
6+ years of experience in product management , with a t least 2 years as a Lead or Senior PM owning a product area end-to-end — including strategy, goal-setting, roadmap execution, and KPI accountability.
A systems thinker who builds for scale. You have experience building product infrastructure or platforms — not just features — and you understand how foundational work compounds over time.
Experience working at the intersection of product and marketing, growth, or acquisition. You have a working understanding of how channels like paid search, paid social, or SEO use product surfaces to drive performance, and you're comfortable holding user experience and channel performance goals together.
Strong analytical skills with demonstrated experience in experimentation — designing testing methodology and cadence, not just interpreting results. You know how to build a testing culture and move a team toward data-informed decisions at speed.
Proven ability to build alignment across engineering, design, analytics, and marketing stakeholders. You bring people along through clear thinking and strong communication rather than through authority.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English. You can translate complex product and technical concepts for executive, marketing, and engineering audiences equally well.
Bonus: Experience in a marketplace, e-commerce, or travel business.
Bonus: A background in engineering or data science — particularly valuable given the technical architecture nature of this role.

Work from anywhere in the world for 30 days per year

Our mission is to make GoCardless the best way to pay and be paid. A track record of translating complex customer pain points into successful, high-impact products.
The ability to define a forward-looking product strategy, informed by the latest technological trends.
A strong understanding of data platforms, with the ability to shape technical direction.
Excellent communication skills, capable of explaining technical concepts simply and engagingly to any audience.
A strong data-driven mindset, with the ability to make decisions and build narratives backed by data.
Bonus points: Experience building and scaling intelligent solutions within a fintech environment.

Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs.
