Who We Are
Verkada is transforming how organizations protect their people and places with an integrated, privacy-sensitive AI-powered platform that includes solutions for video security, access control, air quality sensors, alarms, intercoms, and visitor management.
We’ve got serious momentum in the market: more than 30,000 customers (including 100+ of the Fortune 500), a $5.8B valuation , more than $1 billion in annualized bookings, and backing from CapitalG, Sequoia Capital, General Catalyst, Felicis Ventures, Next47 and more. Physical AI is one of the most consequential technology shifts of our time, and Verkada is at the center of it.
You can look at all kinds of communities to see our platform’s impact in the world. It's the retailer that uses our agentic AI to deter theft before it happens. The warehouse that uses AI-powered alerts to make sure its team is protected on the floor with proper PPE. The school that’s alerted to a threat in real-time and triggers a lockdown in seconds, not minutes. We’re rapidly scaling this impact: today, more than 2 million Verkada devices are deployed across 170+ countries.

This position sits on the Business Systems Product team in the CIO organization.
Verkada sells through partners. Two products carry that motion: the Verkada Store (vStore) , where partners quote, price, and order, and the Partner Portal , where partners run their Verkada business — registering deals, tracking orders and renewals, pulling pricebooks and inventory, requesting marketing funds, and reaching the training and enablement they need to sell. You own both. One partner experience, two surfaces.
Verkada's ambition is to be the easiest company in the industry to do business with, and the Store and the Portal are where that promise is either kept or broken. The bar is a system partners choose to use: intuitive enough to need almost no training, useful enough that nobody keeps a side spreadsheet, and scalable enough that order volume can grow faster than the supporting headcount growth.
This is a build role. vStore is homegrown and in active development, and partner self-service ordering is one of the company's primary levers to scale revenue without scaling headcount. You will own the roadmap end to end with a dedicated engineering team. Executives, Sales, Marketing, and Finance are all invested in these products, so success depends as much on building alignment as on shipping.
We are committed to a thriving in-office culture. This role requires you to be onsite at our HQ in San Mateo, CA.

Build streamlined features for pricing configurations, automated approvals, checkout, payments, and fund requests (MDF/JSF) to enable partners to operate without manual intervention.
Take full ownership of strategy, prioritization, PRDs, and user experience for both core partner platforms, from quote-to-order pathways to navigation and identity management.
Hold both products to a product standard, not an internal-tool standard. The honest measure is whether a partner would rather use the Store than call someone, and whether an internal user would rather use it than build a workaround.
Partner with Sales, Channel, Marketing, Finance, Supply Chain, and Deal Desk to translate needs into features and workflow changes across the full partner journey.
Talk to partners directly. Partner AEs, SEs, order admins, and finance admins each use these products differently, and the roadmap should reflect what they do, not what internal stakeholders assume they do.
Lead cross-functional requirements sessions to define functional scope. Surface the unspoken and conflicting requirements, and drive to a decision.
Directly impact key operational metrics—including board-level targets for self-service order adoption, reduced quote cycle times, straight-through order processing, and support ticket deflection across key partner personas.
Recommend changes to development and system standards that improve scalability and reduce maintenance burden.

Bachelor's degree in MIS, CS, Business, or other technical/analytical field.
Minimum 5+ years of experience, ideally including e-commerce, retail systems, or online storefront management.

Experience with marketplace platforms, channel programs, and multi-channel selling.

Experience designing for multiple personas in a single product, where the same surface has to serve a seller, an admin, and a finance user without becoming a compromise for all three.
Exposure to inventory management, fulfillment/logistics, deal desk, sales operations, or revenue operations functions is a plus.
Solid understanding of UI/UX principles and experience partnering with design on storefront and checkout flows; comfortable reviewing wireframes/prototypes and giving informed product feedback.
A track record of building systems people adopt. You can point to something you shipped that replaced a manual process and stuck.
Work ethic: you do what it takes. Equally comfortable owning a task yourself as delegating it.

You call. You wait. You call again. In every other part of your life, you book in seconds. In healthcare, you’re blocked.
We’re here to give power to the patient.
For nearly 20 years, we’ve built the leading healthcare marketplace - helping tens of millions of people find and book the care they need. Now, we’re going further: building our infrastructure beyond Zocdoc’s marketplace to power access to care wherever patients search, from provider websites and insurance directories to search engines, AI platforms, and more.
Healthcare still lacks something every other major consumer industry takes for granted: a seamless way to go from seeking to getting . We don’t want to own the front door to care; there isn't one. We want to make sure all of those doors open when patients are knocking.
Fixing healthcare starts with fixing access to it. And we're still just getting started.

Healthcare should work for patients, but it doesn’t. In their time of need, they call down outdated insurance directories. Then wait on hold. Then wait weeks for the privilege of a visit. Then wait in a room solely designed for waiting. Then wait for a surprise bill. In any other consumer industry, the companies delivering such a poor customer experience would not survive. But in healthcare, patients lack market power. Which means they are expected to accept the unacceptable.
Zocdoc’s mission is to give power to the patient. To do that, we’ve built the leading healthcare marketplace that makes it easy to find and book in-person or virtual care in all 50 states, across +200 specialties and +12k insurance plans. By giving patients the ability to see and choose, we give them power.

In doing so, we can make healthcare work like every other consumer sector, where businesses compete for customers, not the other way around. In time, this will drive quality up and prices down.
We’re 18 years old and the leader in our space, but we are still just getting started. If you like solving important, complex problems alongside deeply thoughtful, driven, and collaborative teammates, read on.

We Breathe Life Into Data
At Komodo Health, our mission is to reduce the global burden of disease. And we believe that smarter use of data is essential to this mission.

That’s why we built the Healthcare Map — the industry’s largest, most complete, precise view of the U.S. healthcare system — by combining de-identified, real-world patient data with innovative algorithms and decades of clinical experience.

The Healthcare Map serves as our foundation for a powerful suite of software applications, helping us answer healthcare’s most complex questions for our partners.

Across the healthcare ecosystem, we’re helping our clients unlock critical insights to track detailed patient behaviors and treatment patterns, identify gaps in care, address unmet patient needs, and reduce the global burden of disease.
As we pursue these goals, it remains essential to us that we stay grounded in our values: be awesome, seek growth, deliver “wow,” and enjoy the ride. At Komodo, you will be joining a team of ambitious, supportive Dragons with diverse backgrounds but a shared passion to deliver on our mission to reduce the burden of disease — and enjoy the journey along the way.
The Opportunity at Komodo Health
Komodo Health's AI Platform and Services organization builds the platform every AI product at Komodo runs on: agent infrastructure, evals, data context, and the surfaces customers touch. Small pods build on shared primitives and ship in weeks. Product managers here build the first versions of what they propose and to iterate alongside their teams quickly.
The suite that built this business was designed for an analyst at a screen. The platform underneath it now reasons. Our flagship product Navigator runs investigations that used to take a person weeks, and an ai-augmented product suite interoperates with it to streamline workflows. We are just getting started. What the next generation of the suite actually is remains an open question, and today it needs ownership.
That question is this seat. You will define the next generation of Komodo's product suite and prove it by building it. The current surfaces are your material and your distribution. The mandate is what comes after them. Principal here means your answer sets the pattern for every surface that follows.
Looking back on your first 12 months at Komodo Health, you will have…
Put a thesis on record for what the next generation of the suite is, argued in working software customers have touched, and won cross-functional and leadership support for it.
Built the first version of at least two new products from that thesis yourself, then ran a pod of four or fewer from prototype to GA with no dedicated project management.
Those products live in customer environments, with measurable revenue, adoption, or retention impact.
Made the current suite smaller. At least one existing legacy solution retired or folded into its successor, without customer churn.
You will accomplish these outcomes through the following responsibilities:
Own the thesis for what customers touch. Study how they actually work, decide what should exist, and revise the argument as models improve.
Build first versions with AI tools and platform primitives. Bring engineering in to scale what shows value, and drop what does not.
Deploy forward. Work inside customer environments where necessary, scope in real time during contracting cycles, and treat deployment as part of the product.
Propose and defend the shape of the growing portfolio. As the new generation lands, you decide what the existing solutions become.
Set the pattern. Your architecture and your build habits become how the surface pods around you work.

s.h: What you bring to Komodo Health (required)
s.t:
Builds the first version. You will show us something you built, not something you managed, and the interview includes building.
AI native at product depth. You can reason at a low level about the AI products you intend to ship: context and grounding, evals and quality gates, agent behavior, and cost. Using chat tools to work faster is the baseline everywhere, so it earns nothing here.
Forward deployed instinct. Comfortable inside customer environments and contracting cycles, with the judgment to commit responsibly in real time.
Zero to one at Principal scope. 9+ years in product, including at least one product you conceived and shipped that earns real revenue today. We will ask what existed before it, and what was retired to make room for it.
Excellent written communication. Your reasoning gets adopted because it is clear.
Ability to leverage AI tools (Gemini, ChatGPT, Cursor, etc.) to enhance personal productivity, streamline workflows, or improve decision-making

s.h: Additional skills and experience we’d prioritize (nice to have)…
s.t:
Healthcare or regulated data experience (claims, EHR, patient journeys, provider analytics). Time at a company through a platform transition. Experience retiring a product without losing its customers.
Experience interacting with, managing, or building with AI agentic workflows

Attentive’s Data Platform collects and stores data on behalf of our brands across many verticals, from our roots in e-commerce to physical retail, sports, entertainment, travel, and hospitality. Retail brands with physical stores want product inventory modeled down to the store location.

Multinational brands want product catalogs and their customers segregated by market. A sports franchise wants live events and ticketing data modeled so that marketing agents know the right time and context to personalize messaging for any customer.
All the data clients want to ingest into the Attentive platform is activated across our product surface areas, from our core SMS & email products to our next-generation suite of marketing agents.
As the Senior Product Manager, Data Platform Extensibility, you will own the evolution of the Attentive data model to support these use cases. Your mandate is to build the generic primitives that let Attentive model any customer's business in our platform.

You will decide which data entities become first-class concepts in the platform and which stay flexible to meet other customer needs.

This role requires deep technical fluency in data modeling to recognize patterns across seemingly disconnected use cases to identify solutions that can scale across a broad set of verticals that Attentive will expand rapidly into.
What You’ll Accomplish
Introduce new first-class and generic data objects to the data platform, starting with the gaps slowing down enterprise deals today, and establish the paradigm that makes each subsequent object dramatically cheaper to add.
Define how objects relate to one another — users to offers, events to catalogs, catalogs to stores and regions — unlocking use cases like bring-your-own product and offer recommendations that customers cannot express in the platform today.
Build the semantic layer that tells marketers and agents what their data means, and decide what data gets promoted to native object entities
Partner across product and engineering to ensure every new object and field is consistently exposed to segmentation, personalization, reporting, and our APIs and MCP surfaces — so both marketers and agents can reason over and act on it.
Your Expertise
4+ years of product management experience building complex B2B or SaaS platforms, with a track record of owning ambiguous, high-scope problem spaces end to end.
Strong technical fluency with data models and schemas — you can go deep with engineers on storage, relationships, extensibility, and migration tradeoffs, and you understand how an API contract shapes what customers can and cannot do.
Ability to translate abstract infrastructure investment into concrete customer outcomes and business impact that executives and sellers can act on.

Our Payments team⭐
Payments is at the heart of Monzo. It’s how our customers move, receive, spend and manage their money, from cards and bank transfers to cross-border payments, merchant acquiring, payment experiences in the app, and the platform infrastructure that underpins the whole bank.
This role sits in our Payments Platform area, working most closely with our Finance Infrastructure squad. The squad sits in Payments, but partners deeply with Finance teams to build the systems, abstractions and capabilities Monzo needs to operate safely, scale efficiently, and expand into new markets.

You’ll work on foundational financial infrastructure: the ledgers, data, controls, reporting, reconciliation and platform capabilities that help Monzo understand, account for and manage money across the bank.
This is a role for someone who gets genuinely excited by complex, technical infrastructure. The work is often behind the scenes, but it’s business-critical: it helps Monzo scale, launch new products and markets, support Finance, and keep the bank running safely.
🔑You’ll play a key role by...
Defining the product strategy and roadmap for Finance Infrastructure within Payments Platform.
Partnering closely with Engineering, Finance and Payments leaders to understand what Monzo needs from its financial systems today and as we scale.
Moving the team from reactive delivery towards a more strategic, product-led approach, asking why we’re building things, what good looks like, and how today’s choices support Monzo’s long-term needs.
Translating complex finance, accounting, operational and regulatory needs into scalable platform capabilities.
Prioritising across competing stakeholder needs, balancing urgent delivery with long-term system health.
Helping Monzo build financial infrastructure that can support multiple products, entities, countries, currencies and regulatory environments.
Building trusted relationships with senior stakeholders across Finance, Engineering, Product and Operations.
Bringing strong product discipline, technical curiosity and systems thinking to a space that is critical to Monzo’s future growth.

You’re a strong senior Product Manager with experience owning complex technical, platform, infrastructure or financial systems.
You have enough technical depth to partner credibly with engineers and reason about systems, trade-offs, dependencies and long-term architecture.
You’re excited by “boring but critical” infrastructure, things like ledgers, reconciliation, financial data, controls, reporting, internal platforms, abstractions or backend systems.
You can work with senior and cross-functional stakeholders, including Finance, Engineering, Product and operational teams.
You’re comfortable bringing product thinking into ambiguous or stakeholder-heavy environments, and moving teams from request-led delivery towards long-term strategy.
You’re high-agency, ambitious and excited to stretch yourself in a team with a high bar.
You care about customers and business outcomes, even when the work is several layers removed from the end customer experience.

With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless, interest-free installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible.

We’re not just transforming payments; we’re redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values.

As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we’re building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey.

If you’re excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping!

We are seeking a talented and motivated Senior Technical Product Manager who is best in class with a high IQ plus a high EQ. This role presents an exciting opportunity to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment within a rapidly growing team, with abundant prospects for career advancement.
Sezzle is building the platform that will carry us from a BNPL provider into a full-stack financial institution. This role owns the system at the center of that: Sezzle’s banking core — the ledger, accounts and balances, and the money movement that every future Sezzle financial product will run on.
You would own it end to end. Discovery, architecture and vendor decisions, requirements, build, launch, and everything after — not a slice of someone else’s roadmap, but the full product lifecycle for the platform itself. You’d work directly with Engineering, Finance, Compliance, Treasury, and Risk, with real authority over how this gets built.
Ideally you’ve built something like this before. If you haven’t, but you’ve owned a ledger, a payments platform, an issuing program, or other financial infrastructure — and you’re the kind of person who learns a domain properly rather than around the edges — we want to talk to you. What matters most is that you’ve owned real infrastructure and that you’re willing to go deep on the parts you don’t know yet.

Own the banking platform roadmap. Define and sequence the platform work required to support accounts, deposits, cards, and lending on a single ledger and account model.
Help drive the build-vs-buy decision. Evaluate core banking platforms and processors, run vendor diligence, model cost and time-to-market, and help leadership decide whether we extend what we have or integrate a third party.
Shape the account and ledger model. Work with Engineering and Finance on account hierarchies, sub-ledgers, chart-of-accounts mapping, posting rules, holds, interest and fee accrual, and general ledger integration.
Specify money movement. Own product requirements for transfers, ACH, card issuing and network settlement, real-time rails, and returns and reversals — including exception handling, cutoff windows, and settlement reconciliation.
Make the platform auditable. Ensure the system produces the reporting, traceability, and controls that Finance, audit, and regulators need — reconciliation breaks, balance attestation, and complete transaction history.
Partner on regulatory readiness. Work with Compliance and Legal to turn their requirements into platform capabilities: screening hooks, onboarding data, error resolution, disclosures and statements, and reporting. You don’t need to arrive fluent in US banking regulation — you do need to be someone who learns it properly.
Plan migration and cutover. If a migration is in scope, own data mapping, parallel-run strategy, validation criteria, rollback plans, and phased cutover.
Write the technical requirements. Own detailed specs, API contracts, event schemas, data models, user stories, and release plans end-to-end.
Use data to prove it works. Write your own SQL. Define platform KPIs — posting latency, reconciliation break rate, settlement accuracy, failure rates — and monitor them relentlessly.
Manage risk early. Anticipate technical risks, edge cases, race conditions, and dependencies before they become incidents. Money movement defects are the expensive kind.
Operate with urgency. Deliver against an evolving regulatory and business timeline with incomplete information.

Bachelor’s or advanced degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or other technical discipline (required).
5–10 years of product experience, with meaningful time spent on financial infrastructure rather than only customer-facing surfaces.
Real ownership in at least one of the following. You do not need all of them, and we care much more about depth in one than exposure to several:
Ledgers, general ledger, or balance and transaction systems
Payments processing, orchestration, or money movement — ACH, card networks, transfers, settlement, or the LATAM equivalents (PIX, SPEI, PSE, CCE)
Card issuing or card program management
Deposit, wallet, or account platforms
Lending origination or loan servicing platforms
Product work at a processor, BaaS provider, or core banking vendor
Comfort with double-entry accounting concepts as they show up in software — debits and credits, sub-ledgers, accruals, reconciliation — or a genuine appetite to get comfortable with them quickly.
Deep technical understanding of APIs, event-driven architecture, idempotency, distributed system failure modes, batch vs. real-time processing, and data flows.
Strong SQL skills and comfort querying and interpreting data independently.
Experience working directly with Compliance, Legal, Finance, or Treasury as stakeholders — not only Engineering and Design.
Comfortable working in ambiguity and making sound, documented decisions with incomplete information.
Strong written and verbal communication — can hold your own in an engineering standup, a Finance review, and an executive discussion.
Hands-on familiarity with AI tools, data models, or generative AI applications—personally, professionally, or better yet, both!

Direct experience with a core banking platform, in-house or vendor (Thought Machine, Mambu, 10x, Finxact, Temenos, Technisys, Galileo, Pismo, or similar).
Experience with a core migration, conversion, or major ledger replacement.
Experience at a chartered or licensed financial institution, or supporting a charter, banking licence, or deposit insurance application.
Familiarity with consumer finance regulation — US (Reg E, Reg DD, Reg CC, Reg Z, TILA, FCRA, BSA/AML) or equivalent local regimes.
Background in consumer credit or BNPL, card products, or bank-fintech sponsorship programs.
Experience with third-party risk management and vendor oversight in a regulated environment.

Buscamos una persona que sea el puente entre las soluciones de AI que construimos y los problemas de negocio reales de nuestros clientes. Este rol es responsable de entender el problema del cliente a fondo, identificar la mejor forma de resolverlo y acompañar todo el proceso hasta que la solución se adopte de forma efectiva y medible dentro de la operación del cliente.
No es un rol de ingeniería ni de gestión de equipos técnicos: es el rol que garantiza que la tecnología resuelva el problema correcto, de la forma correcta, para las personas correctas.
Responsabilidades
Entender en profundidad el problema de negocio del cliente a través de entrevistas con usuarios y stakeholders, y del mapeo real de su flujo de trabajo.
Liderar el proceso de discovery en cada cuenta asignada.
Liderar la adaptación de soluciones de Monks (o liderar nuevos desarrollos cuando sea necesario) para las necesidades descubiertas
Desarrollar un prototipo inicial utilizando herramientas de AI, validarlo con usuarios reales y traducir los hallazgos en requerimientos claros para el equipo técnico.
Revisar el avance del desarrollo junto al cliente, identificando y priorizando ajustes o mejoras a partir de feedback real.
Liderar el entrenamiento de los equipos usuarios, acompañar el lanzamiento y coordinar la resolución de incidencias junto al equipo técnico.
Documentar la adopción real de cada solución a través de casos de uso concretos, presentables al cliente.
Identificar y elevar nuevas oportunidades de negocio que surjan dentro de la cuenta, colaborando con el leadership en su evaluación y priorización.
Recopilar y priorizar ideas para futuras fases de cada solución.
Comunicar avances, riesgos y trade-offs con claridad al leadership.
Requisitos
Experiencia comprobable liderando procesos de discovery e investigación de usuarios, con foco en traducir problemas de negocio en soluciones concretas.
Fluidez en el uso de herramientas de IA (Claude, ChatGPT u otras) para prototipado rápido. No se requiere experiencia en programación, pero sí un uso activo y cotidiano de estas herramientas como parte del flujo de trabajo.
Experiencia liderando procesos de onboarding, capacitación o adopción de producto con clientes finales.
Excelentes habilidades de comunicación y manejo de relaciones con cliente: reuniones, presentaciones y gestión de expectativas.
Capacidad de traducir necesidades de negocio en requerimientos claros y accionables para equipos de ingeniería.
Español nativo o avanzado; inglés profesional avanzado.
Valorado: experiencia previa en consultoría, agencias de marketing, o roles de solutions/customer success con componente técnico.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Tavily, part of Nebius, is the web access layer for AI agents. Over two million developers use us, and our customers include Fortune 500 companies running agents in production.
You will own our enterprise product: the roadmap for what large customers need, and the control plane that makes it possible. These are the capabilities that decide whether a large customer can adopt us, trust us, and expand with us.
Our product is an API, and our enterprise buyer is an engineering organization. The people you build for are platform teams, architects, and the developers inside those companies who are putting agents into production. You need to be comfortable making product decisions about API surfaces, developer workflows, and technical tradeoffs, not only about business requirements.
To build this well, you have to be in the room. You will work alongside customer success, sales, and our forward-deployed engineers, who are in these accounts every week and already know where we fall short, and you will spend real time with customers alongside them. Delivery and implementation stay with forward-deployed engineering and go-to-market. Your job is to turn what you learn into product.
The hard part is judgment. Knowing which request is one account's edge case, and which one is the thing every enterprise customer will ask for six months from now. Getting that right is the difference between a platform and a pile of custom work.
In your first year, we expect you to own a clear enterprise roadmap, ship the controls that block deals today, and become the person the go-to-market team comes to before a deal gets stuck.
This is a hands-on senior IC role with real ownership, reporting to the Director of Product. The product team is small, so you will work directly with the engineers building your roadmap and with the go-to-market teams selling it.

Own the enterprise roadmap: what we build for large customers, in what order, and why.
Own the platform behind it: organizations and identity, keys and quotas, spend controls, usage observability and audit, policy enforcement, and data residency.
Make product decisions on our API surface for enterprise use, so that the developers inside those accounts can build on us without friction.
Work with customer success, sales, and forward-deployed engineering to understand what enterprise customers need, and spend time in accounts alongside them to see it first hand.
Tell the difference between a single-account request and a pattern worth building for, and be able to defend the call either way.
Hand off what belongs to another product area, with the evidence that makes it actionable.
Give sales and marketing the positioning, materials, and product understanding they need to sell a technical product well.
Represent enterprise customers in roadmap decisions with evidence rather than anecdote.
We expect you to have
6+ years of product management experience, with a meaningful part of it spent on enterprise products in B2B, developer platform, or API businesses.
Experience building developer-facing or API products, with real understanding of what makes an API good to build against.

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.
Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.
Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

Tavily, part of Nebius, is the web access layer for AI agents. Over two million developers use us, and our customers include Fortune 500 companies running agents in production.
We build and run our own index. That means we own the hard problems directly: crawl coverage at scale, freshness, cost per query, and the quality of what comes back. This role owns that infrastructure as a product.
When an agent asks a question, the answer has to be relevant, fresh, fast, and affordable. Those four things pull against each other, and someone has to decide which one gives. That is you. You will set what good means for each use case we serve and the bar a change has to clear before it ships, working closely with our evaluation team, who own how we measure it. You will also shape where our index goes next: what it needs to cover, how fresh it needs to be, and what it has to be good at.
The most open part of the job is what comes next. Search is being rebuilt for a consumer that is not a person. Agents do not want one result page, they want to break a problem apart, run many retrievals, and decide what to do next. That changes what search infrastructure should look like, and part of your job is to have a view on where ours should go.
The hard part is deciding what good enough means. Perfect coverage, perfect freshness, and low cost cannot all be true at once, and the person in this seat is the one who has to make that call for each use case and defend it.
In your first year, we expect you to set a clear quality bar for our search products that the team builds against, have a real influence on where our index goes next, and bring us a point of view on where search infrastructure is heading.
This is a hands-on senior IC role with real ownership, reporting to the Director of Product. You will work day to day with our search engineering and research teams, with the evaluation team, and with customer success, who bring us quality feedback from real accounts every week.

Our search engineers are deeply experienced in large-scale retrieval, and the product team is small, so you will argue your case directly with the people building it. That only works if you have built at this scale yourself.

Set the quality bar and release criteria for search: what good means per use case, and what a change has to clear before it ships. Our evaluation team owns the measurement, and you work closely with them on what to measure and why.
Own the depth, latency, and cost tradeoffs across our search products, and make them explicit and defensible.
Shape the direction of our index: what it needs to cover, how fresh it needs to be, and what quality bar it has to meet.
Build a point of view on where search infrastructure is going as agents, rather than people, become the main consumer, and turn that into a roadmap.
Know how we compare to the alternatives customers evaluate, and drive the work that closes the gaps that matter.
Work with customer success and directly with customers to understand where our results fall short in real workflows, and turn that into quality priorities.
Partner with the data and vertical product owners on what our corpus needs to contain and how results should be shaped per industry.

FX Senior Product Manager - Hedging conversion
Ebury London Office - Hybrid: 4 days in the office, 1 day working from home per week
As Ebury scales globally, we are evolving from a delivery-led organisation into a platform-led product company - building shared foundations that allow teams to move faster, operate safely in regulated environments and deliver high-quality client experiences across channel
The Opportunity
We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to own one number: the share of Ebury's clients who convert into hedgers — and to build the journeys, workflows and decision tools that get them there.
Ebury has a real hedging business. Thousands of clients already hedge with us, they're our most valuable and stickiest, and Hedge works. The problem isn't proof of concept — it's rate. For every client who converts, several more carry the same currency exposure, would benefit from the same forward, and never get there.
Here's the honest reason why. Hedging isn't a product you sell; it's a conclusion a client reaches once they can see what their international business is actually exposed to. Today that seeing happens in a CPM's head and a spreadsheet, one client at a time. The client can't see their own exposure clearly, the CPM can't see it at scale, and so the conversation that should be obvious either happens late or never happens at all.
This role builds the layer that changes that: guided journeys and lifecycle workflows that carry a client from unaware exposure to a first hedge to a standing policy — and the decision tools that let both the client and their CPM understand the client's international business well enough to make the right call, not just the next call.
You'll sit at the intersection of product, data, and commercial, working closely with:
CPMs and Sales teams who convert clients today
Data and Analytics
Design and Engineering
Compliance and Risk
Clients directly

You will own the end-to-end conversion journey into hedging, backed by a dedicated squad of developers, including:
Journeys & Lifecycle Workflows
The path from spot client → Hedge-active → policy client, and every drop-off point along it
Guided, staged journeys rather than one-off prompts: the right message, to the right client, at the moment their exposure is real to them
Triggered workflows off real events, a new currency pair, a large invoice, a rate move against them, a forward maturing
Understanding what separates the clients who convert from the ones who don't, and building for the difference
Decision Tools for Clients
Showing a client what their international business is actually exposed to, in their own numbers and their own currencies
Exposure views, scenario and impact modelling, MTM and forward comparisons a finance lead can act on without training
Turning "should I hedge?" into a question the client can answer for themselves, with confidence
Balancing honesty about risk against simplicity of decision, the goal is a well-made decision, not a sold one
Tooling for CPMs
Giving CPMs a portfolio-level view of client exposure, trades and performance, so they know who to talk to and what to say before the client asks
Surfacing the signals that make a conversation timely: unhedged exposure, changing trade patterns, policy lapses
Learning from the conversations that already convert clients, and productising them
Repeat Hedging & Policy
Turning a first hedge into a second and a third
Moving clients from ad-hoc trades onto a standing hedging policy they run every month
Statements, notifications and review moments that build the habit and prove the value after the fact
Experimentation & Measurement
A cadence of A/B tests across the journey, not a feature backlog
Reading results honestly, including the ones that kill your own ideas
Building the measurement so conversion, and what's driving it
What success looks like (12-18 months)
Spot-to-hedger conversion rate is measurably higher, and you can attribute the lift
A meaningful share of new hedgers convert through product journeys rather than a CPM conversation
CPMs work from exposure signals in a tool instead of instinct and spreadsheets, and cover more clients as a result
Clients can articulate their own FX exposure — and clients who hedge once come back without being called
More hedgers move onto hedging policies rather than trading ad hoc
Product — not people — becomes the primary driver of hedging conversion
What makes this role hard
You're changing behaviour, not shipping features. The instrument already exists and works; the reason more clients don't use it is understanding, trust and habit.
It's a two-sided problem. Clients and CPMs need different views of the same truth, and building for one badly makes the other worse but the CPMs must know what the client can see to have consultative conversations
The baseline isn't zero. There's an existing business and an existing way of converting clients, you have to improve on it without disrupting it.
Exposure is genuinely hard to model. Client data is incomplete, trade history is a proxy for intent, and being confidently wrong about someone's exposure destroys trust instantly.
You're helping non-experts make decisions with real financial consequences. Oversimplify and you mislead; don't simplify and nobody acts.
You'll navigate real-world complexity: regional and regulatory nuance, credit and margin implications, and client segments with genuinely different needs.

Prior FX or hedging experience is a plus, not a requirement. We're looking for someone who can move a hard conversion number in a complex, regulated environment — with strong agency, sharp analytical instincts, and a real feel for why people do and don't act.

4+ years of product management experience, including at least one role owning conversion, adoption or engagement outcomes end-to-end
Strong analytics and experimentation skills — funnel analysis, cohort and retention analysis, designing and interpreting A/B tests
Experience designing lifecycle journeys or triggered workflows, and the messaging that carries them
Fluent English (daily collaboration with global commercial, tech and Legal/Compliance/Risk stakeholders)

Familiarity with foreign exchange, hedging or other asset classes
Experience in fintech or regulated financial products
Experience building internal or advisor-facing tooling alongside client-facing product
Localisation awareness
Core Capabilities
Strong Product Fundamentals — breaks down ambiguous problems into clear product opportunities; comfortable working across UX, data and operations; focused on outcomes, not just delivery.

CRM Voice AI builds autonomous voice agents for customer service that resolve customer interactions end-to-end and drive significant value for the business. We're a team inside ServiceNow's CRM business unit, shipping production voice AI with enterprise customers today and scaling aggressively.

Our agents run on a real-time streaming pipeline with best-in-class orchestration, integrated into the same platform where many of our customers already manage their front, middle, and back-office workflows. For those that don't, the voice agent is often the tip of the spear that brings them in.

We compete directly against well-funded AI startups and CCaaS incumbents, and we're winning.

We work in pods - small, dedicated teams embedded with a single enterprise customer, building their voice agents from first call to self-sufficiency.

A pod owns the full lifecycle: agent shadowing, conversation design, build, production go-live, monitoring and optimization and the handoff that makes the customer self-sufficient so the pod can move on to the next one.

Each pod pairs forward-deployed engineers with a product manager who owns both the customer outcome and the product learning that comes from it.
Every PM on this team runs at least one pod directly and has visibility across others. You're in the customer's world - on their calls, in their systems, solving their problems - while simultaneously shaping what the product becomes. The learnings from your pods feed directly into the platform roadmap and into repeatable, productized assets that scale beyond any single customer.

You run one pod directly and float across one to two others, providing product direction and unblocking teams. You own the relationship with the customer’s leadership team, setting the timelines and expectations, then delivering on them.
For those pods, you and your team of FDEs own agent design, the build and evaluation.
Beyond your pods, you own STT and TTS model evaluation and experimentation for CRM Voice AI. The speech model landscape is moving fast. New ASR and TTS models ship constantly, each with different tradeoffs on latency, accuracy, naturalness, language support, and cost.

You run structured evaluations against real production workloads, collaborate closely with the platform voice team on model decisions, and drive experimentation across our customer base.

When a new model drops and the question is "should we move our customers to this?" - you're the one with the methodology, the data, and the production context to answer it.
You also support a variety of industry verticals. As you see patterns across your pods and model evaluations, you identify which capabilities and conversation designs can be prioritized and productized for a specific industry, building the playbook for how CRM Voice AI enters a new market.

s.h: Why This and Not Somewhere Else
s.t:
The pod model means you’ll accumulate more production voice AI experience in a year than most PMs get in several - building agents across different industries, different contact center environments, and different conversation types.

On top of that, speech models are the most dynamic layer of the voice AI stack right now, and most PMs evaluating them do it in a lab. You're doing it against real production traffic with enterprise customers who have real SLAs.

You sit at the intersection of the platform team building the voice infrastructure and the CRM team deploying it, with influence in both directions. The right evaluation methodology is a genuine competitive advantage, and you're the person building it.

8+ years of product management experience, with recent work in voice AI, conversational AI, or speech technology.
Hands-on experience building and evaluating AI agents - conversation design, prompt engineering, testing and iteration against real user interactions. This is the foundation; speech model expertise layers on top of it.
Working knowledge of speech models - ASR architectures, TTS synthesis approaches, and the tradeoffs between latency, accuracy, naturalness, and cost. You've evaluated or deployed these in production, not just prototyped.
Comfort with experimentation and evaluation methodology. You know how to design a test, instrument it, and turn the results into a product decision.
Experience with telephony integration: SIP, call transfers, IVR systems, or CCaaS platforms.
Experience working directly with enterprise customers on technical products.
Ability to context-switch between deep technical model evaluation and customer-facing product work without dropping either.

Hands-on experience benchmarking across multiple ASR or TTS providers.
Background in machine learning or audio/speech engineering, enough to hold your own in model architecture discussions.
Industry expertise in verticals with high contact center volume: telecommunications, financial services, travel, healthcare.
